author: ani67
body:
## Summary

Two major improvements: (1) training speed fixes that took the model from frozen at 600+ clusters to ~300 steps/sec, and (2) a frontend audit that added live dashboard metrics and fixed type mismatches.

## Performance fixes

The model was freezing above 500 clusters because each batch of 32 samples ran 32 independent BFS graph walks, rebuilt the identity matrix from scratch, and scanned all clusters for updates. At 600+ clusters with 10K+ edges, this was billions of operations per batch.

### What changed

- **Diff-based identity matrix**: persistent `(N, 512)` tensor, only ~20 changed rows patched per step instead of rebuilding all 600
- **Cached traversal order**: BFS computed once per batch, reused for all 32 samples (eliminates 31 redundant graph walks)
- **Vectorized resonance**: 600 sequential Python dot products → 1 matrix-vector multiply
- **Targeted FF updates**: iterate ~20 visited clusters instead of scanning all 600
- **Targeted snapshots**: snapshot ~20 visited clusters instead of all 600
- **Identity cache on Cluster**: `@property` recomputed every call → cached, invalidated on `ff_update()`
- **Growth cap on INSERT + EXTEND**: was only blocking BUD at 500 clusters, INSERT kept going to 695

### Benchmark at 660 clusters

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Batch (32 samples) | >10 seconds (frozen) | 88-112ms |
| Steps/sec | 0 | 286-362 |
| BFS per batch | 32 full walks | 1 walk + 32 cached replays |

## Frontend audit

### New: Dashboard metrics panel
- Floating overlay on latent space (bottom-right), polls `/dashboard` every 5s
- Shows: spatial score, co-firing communities, buffer stats, category performance, growth rate
- Collapsible to "M" button, matches existing design language

### Fixed: DeltaMessage TypeScript interface
- Added missing fields: `step`, `stage`, `dialogue`, `growth_events`, `graph_summary`
- Exported interface for reuse

### Fixed: Dead code removed
- Removed 33 lines of unreachable `msg.type === 'step'` handler (backend never sends this type)
- Cleaned up 3 unused store selector imports

### Added: Dashboard API endpoint
- Fully typed `api.dashboard()` method

## Files changed

```
Backend:
  backend/model/baby_model.py  — diff identity matrix, cached traversal,
                                 vectorized resonance, targeted updates,
                                 growth cap on INSERT/EXTEND
  backend/model/cluster.py     — identity cache with invalidation

Frontend:
  frontend/src/components/MetricsPanel.tsx  — NEW: live metrics overlay
  frontend/src/App.tsx                      — mount MetricsPanel
  frontend/src/lib/api.ts                   — dashboard() endpoint
  frontend/src/store/graphStore.ts          — fix DeltaMessage interface
  frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts        — remove dead code
  frontend/src/styles/global.css            — metrics panel styles
```

## Experiment status

Buffer experiment validated across 22K steps (clean data):
- Spatial score: 0.079 → 0.227 (peak), holding at 0.179
- Co-firing communities: 1 → 12 (blob split for the first time ever)
- Second community growing: 28 → 40 members
- Growth stabilized at 695 clusters (cap active)
- Ready for Phase B (multi-prototype clusters) when spatial plateaus

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 -c "import model.baby_model"` — syntax clean
- [x] Vectorized resonance matches sequential results
- [x] Identity cache: hit on second access, invalidated after ff_update
- [x] Diff matrix: only dirty rows refreshed, full rebuild on cluster count change
- [x] Cached traversal: batch produces same results as individual forwards
- [x] Benchmark: 286-362 steps/sec at 660 clusters (was frozen)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — TypeScript clean
- [x] `npx vite build` — build clean

author: copilot
body:
Full stack migration: Bun/Elysia/Docker → Deno/Hono/Cloudflare Workers with Neon serverless driver for database access.

### Runtime & Framework
- **Elysia.js → Hono**: All 17 API endpoints preserved with identical routing (`/api/v1/*`)
- **Bun → Deno** for local dev, **Cloudflare Workers** for production
- Entry point exports default Hono app (CF Workers pattern); `src/dev.ts` wraps with `Deno.serve()` for local dev

### Database
- **pg (node-postgres) → @neondatabase/serverless**: HTTP-based driver, no connection pool needed
- Uses `neon()` with `arrayMode: true` + `sql.query()` for parameterized queries

```typescript
// Before (pg pool + client)
const result = await client.query<IdRecord>(
  { rowMode: "array", text: "SELECT pgmq.send($1::text, $2::jsonb, $3::integer)" },
  [queue_name, msg, delay],
);

// After (neon HTTP driver)
const sql = getSQL(c.env.DATABASE_URL);
const rows = await sql.query("SELECT pgmq.send($1::text, $2::jsonb, $3::integer)", [queue_name, JSON.stringify(msg), delay]);
```

### Deployment
- **Docker → Cloudflare Workers** via `wrangler.toml`
- `DATABASE_URL` as single env var (Wrangler secret) replaces six separate `DB_*` vars
- Removed: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, Docker CI workflow

### Config & Tooling
- `deno.json` replaces `tsconfig.json` + `eslint.config.mjs` (Deno has built-in linter/formatter)
- `package.json` retained (minimal) for wrangler/npm resolution with `nodeModulesDir: "auto"`
- Swagger UI via `@hono/swagger-ui` with inline OpenAPI spec

### Tests & CI
- `bun:test` → `Deno.test()` + `node:assert/strict` (no JSR dependency needed)
- CI: Deno lint + type check; integration tests gated on `DATABASE_URL` availability

## Description

When creating a new EA using `yarn new`, it currently (since https://github.com/smartcontractkit/external-adapters-js/pull/4349) uses the framework version of `packages/scripts`. This might not be the newest version.

This PR changes it to use the newest framework version among versions already used int he repo.

But it keeps the behavior to use the `packages/scripts` version of that's a portal version, because it's used for testing when making changes to the generator.

## Changes

1. Add helper function `getFrameworkVersionSpecFromRepo` to determine the framework version to use.
2. Use it.

## Steps to Test

1. `yarn new` and follow instructions.
2. Check the framework version in the generated package.
3. Make some changes in the local framework repo
4. Create a portal dependency following  [these steps](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/external-adapters-js/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#framework-development).
5. `yarn new` and follow instructions.
6. Check that the generated packages has the changes from step 3.

### Motivation

- Allow public/direct captures to upload the actual video binary so backend can resolve media and run the multimodal pipeline instead of falling back to placeholders.
- Maintain backward compatibility with the existing JSON-only metadata upload path.

### Description

- Add multipart/form-data handling to the upload endpoint by changing `attach_recording_endpoint` to accept a `Request`, detect `multipart/form-data`, parse form fields, accept a `video_file` part and build an `UploadRecordingRequest` from it, or fall back to JSON payload parsing for legacy clients.
- Add `_parse_capture_meta` to safely parse `capture_meta` JSON and return meaningful `400` responses on invalid JSON.
- Implement `persist_uploaded_video_blob` in `comunicacion/services/recording_service.py` to write uploaded bytes to a temporary directory (`/tmp/comunicacion_uploads`) and return a `file://`-style `video_ref`, inferring `.mp4` vs `.webm` from filename or mime hint.
- Update frontend `backend/comunicacion_app/app.js` to send `FormData` with `video_file` for the nominal path and fall back to JSON metadata-only upload if the binary upload fails.
- Add tests that exercise real multipart uploads, backend persistence, pipeline bundle building for resolved files, and diagnosis of the client-temp fallback behavior in `backend/tests/test_communication_public_upload_real_video.py` and `backend/tests/test_communication_railway_direct_placeholder_diagnosis.py`.
- Add documentation describing the diagnosis and the chosen solution for Railway/direct deployments.

Files changed: `backend/comunicacion/api/router.py`, `backend/comunicacion/services/recording_service.py`, `backend/comunicacion_app/app.js`, new tests under `backend/tests/`, and new docs under `docs/comunicacion/implementacion_multimodal/ejecucion/`.

body:
Resolves #58

This PR implements a storage abstraction layer to support multiple storage vendors in the future.

### Key Changes:
- **Storage Abstraction Interface**: Created `RemoteStorageProvider` interface in `src/storageProviders/RemoteStorageProviderInterface.ts`.
- **Dynamic Provider Registry**: Introduced `StorageProviderRegistry` to manage available storage providers and resolve them by ID.
- **Consolidated Implementation**: Moved all Google Drive-specific logic from `googleService.ts` directly into `GoogleDriveProvider.ts` to reduce indirection and simplify the architecture. `googleService.ts` has been removed.
- **Generic Sync Hook**: Refactored `useGoogleSync` into a provider-agnostic `useRemoteSync` hook that delegates vendor-specific logic (like OAuth callback parsing) to the provider.
- **UI Updates**: 
    - `SettingsModal` now includes a provider selection dropdown.
    - Encapsulated vendor-specific configuration (like Google Client ID) within the Settings Modal.
- **Documentation**: Updated `docs/STORAGE_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/features.md` to reflect the new decoupled architecture.
- **Testing**:
    - Replaced concrete provider mocks in hook tests with a `MockStorageProvider`.
    - Created a shared compliance test suite (`runProviderComplianceTests`) to ensure any future provider implementation adheres to the required contract.
    - Expanded `GoogleDriveProvider` tests to cover the consolidated logic (auth refresh, multi-part upload, folder discovery).

- `npm run test` passes (73 tests across all files).
- Manual verification of the UI layout and state management.

body:
## Changes

### Core Fixes
- **Element Energy Calculation**: Replaced incorrect von Mises-based energy formula with proper finite element strain energy computation (∫ σ ⊡ ε dΩ)
- **OC Update**: Removed negative sensitivity guard to use absolute value of sensitivities, allowing all elements to be updated

### API Updates
- Added `cellvalues` parameter to `create_results_data()` function signature for proper energy calculations
- Updated `ResultsData` struct to store `cellvalues` for post-processing

### Propagation
- Updated all 14 example files and test suite to pass `cellvalues` to `create_results_data()` calls
- Updated documentation in README.md

## Impact
Improves optimization accuracy by correctly computing element strain energy and enabling density updates for all elements during optimality criteria iterations.

body:
## Summary

- Add `NotificationDeliveryService` to orchestrate multi-channel notification delivery
- Create email templates for notification types with type-specific styling and colors
- Update all notification handlers (mention, follow, common-ground, moderation) to trigger delivery
- Respect user preferences (`notifyByEmail`, `notifyByPush`) before sending
- Log all delivery attempts to `NotificationLog` for auditing

## Implementation Details

**NotificationDeliveryService** (`notification-delivery.service.ts`):
- Fetches user notification preferences and contact info
- Delivers via email (AWS SES) when `notifyByEmail` is enabled
- Delivers via push (FCM) when `notifyByPush` is enabled and FCM token exists
- Creates audit trail in NotificationLog table

**Email Templates** (`notification.template.ts`):
- Type-specific colors (blue for mentions, purple for follows, green for common ground, amber for moderation)
- Type-specific emojis in subject lines
- HTML version with responsive design and dark mode support
- Plain text fallback version
- XSS protection via HTML escaping

**Delivery Flow**:
1. Handler creates notification in database (existing)
2. Handler emits WebSocket event for real-time delivery (existing)
3. Handler calls `NotificationDeliveryService.deliverNotification()` (new)
4. Service checks user preferences and delivers via enabled channels
5. Delivery is fire-and-forget (non-blocking)

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for `NotificationDeliveryService` (18 tests)
- [x] Unit tests for notification email template (26 tests)
- [x] Existing handler tests updated and passing
- [x] All 125 notification service tests passing

Closes #1123

```markdown
 # Summary                                                                                                                                                              
                            
  Implement authorization (authz) framework with two-level permission system: platform-level and project-level.                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                       
 # Permission System Overview                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                       
 ## Permission Format                                                                                                                                                    
                                                            
  Permissions follow Resource.Action format, e.g., user.read, model.push. Wildcards are supported (e.g., model.* matches all model operations).                        
                                                            
 ### Two-Level Permissions                                                                                                                                                
                                                            
  ┌──────────┬────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┐                                                                                  
  │  Level   │           Scope            │           Example Permissions           │
  ├──────────┼────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                  
  │ Platform │ Global resources           │ user.read, registry.create, sync.update │
  ├──────────┼────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────┤                                                                                  
  │ Project  │ Project-specific resources │ member.add, model.push, dataset.delete  │                                                                                  
  └──────────┴────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┘                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                       
 # How to Add Authorization                                                                                                                                             
                                                            
  1. Platform-Level Authorization (Middleware)                                                                                                                         
                                                            
  Platform permissions are enforced automatically via Gin middleware. Add new paths to permissionPaths in internal/apiserver/middleware/authz.go:                      
                                                            
publicAuthzMethods = map[string]bool{
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.Login/Login":  true,
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.Login/Logout": true,

	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.CurrentUser/GetCurrentUser":    true,
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.CurrentUser/ResetPassword":     true,
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.CurrentUser/ListAccessTokens":  true,
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.CurrentUser/CreateAccessToken": true,
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.CurrentUser/DeleteAccessToken": true,
	"/matrixhub.v1alpha1.CurrentUser/GetProjectRoles":   true,                                                                                                                                                           
        // Add your new Grpc Service paths here...                                                                                                                                
  }                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                            
  2. Project-Level Authorization (Manual)                                                                                                                              
                                                            
  Project permissions require manual verification in the handler. Inject authz.IAuthzService and call:                                                                 
                                                            
  func (h *YourHandler) SomeAction(ctx context.Context, req *pb.Request) (*pb.Response, error) {                                                                       
      // 1. Get projectID first (usually from request parameters)                                                                                                      
      projectID, err := h.projectRepo.GetProjectIDByName(ctx, req.GetName())                                                                                           
      if err != nil {                                                                                                                                                  
          return nil, status.Error(codes.NotFound, err.Error())                                                                                                        
      }                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                       
      // 2. Verify permission                                                                                                                                          
      if allowed, err := h.authzService.VerifyProjectPermission(ctx, projectID, authz.ModelPush); err != nil || !allowed {
          return nil, status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")                                                                                        
      }

author: pranav27sh
body: ### Summary Refactors the voting system to enforce strict isolation between the three terminal flows (Digital, Manual, Token), ensuring each machine operates independently with no cross-navigation or mode-switching capabilities. ### Problem The existing codebase used a shared React Router setup with routes and navigation components that allowed switching between verification flows (e.g., `onSwitchManual` callbacks, `TerminalNav` with links to all three terminals). This was incompatible with the real-world deployment model where each flow runs on a physically separate, dedicated machine. ### Solution Replaced the router-based multi-flow architecture with an environment variable (`VITE_APP_MODE`) that locks each app instance to a single flow at build/deploy time. Removed all cross-flow navigation components, callbacks, and routes. Each terminal now renders only its designated page with no ability to switch modes. ### Key Changes - **`App.tsx`**: Removed `BrowserRouter`/`Routes` entirely; app now reads `VITE_APP_MODE` and renders only the matching page (`DigitalVerifyPage`, `ManualVerifyPage`, or `TokenCheckPage`). Invalid mode values fall back to `'digital'` with a console error. - **`AadhaarVerification.tsx`**: Removed `onSwitchManual` prop and the "Proceed to Manual Desk" button. Replaced with a static message directing voters to contact election officials. - **`BiometricVerification.tsx`**: Removed commented-out `onSwitchManual` prop reference and replaced the "Proceed to Manual Desk" button with the same static guidance message. - **`DigitalVerifyPage.tsx`**: Removed `TerminalNav` and cleaned up `onSwitchManual` pass-throughs to child components. - **`ManualVerifyPage.tsx`**: Removed `TerminalNav`; reset flow no longer resets language selection (language persists across voters on the same terminal). - **`TokenCheckPage.tsx`**: Removed `TerminalNav`; reset flow no longer resets language selection. - **Deleted files**: `TerminalNav.tsx`, `NavLink.tsx`, `TokenGeneration.tsx`, `NotFound.tsx`, `Index.tsx` — all removed as they are no longer needed in the isolated architecture. - **`vite-env.d.ts`**: Added `ImportMetaEnv` type declaration for `VITE_APP_MODE` to ensure type safety across the codebase. ---    --- To clone this PR locally use the [Github CLI](https://cli.github.com/) with command `gh pr checkout 7` You can tag me at @builderio for anything you want me to fix or change

author: copilot
body:
The `/api/auth/check-permission` endpoint was fully unauthenticated, allowing anyone to enumerate system permissions and map the access control structure without credentials.

## Changes

- **Auth guard**: Validates session via `auth.api.getSession` before processing any request; returns `401` immediately for unauthenticated callers
- **Rate limiting**: Enforces 10 req/min per authenticated user using the existing `rateLimit` utility (keyed by `check-permission:<userId>`); returns `429` with `Retry-After` header when exceeded

```ts
// Before — no auth, open to enumeration
export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const { resource, action } = await request.json();
  return NextResponse.json({ hasPermission: await checkPermission(resource, action) });
}

// After
export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() });
  if (!session) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 });

  const rl = rateLimit(`check-permission:${session.user.id}`, { limit: 10, windowSeconds: 60 });
  if (!rl.success) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429, headers: { 'Retry-After': ... } });

  // ... existing permission check
}
```

> **Note**: The rate limiter is in-memory and won't synchronize across multiple serverless instances — a pre-existing limitation already documented in the codebase. A Redis-backed solution is the recommended upgrade path for production scale.

author: daguimu
body:
## Problem

`SchemaDescriptorRegistry` has three thread-safety issues. This class is called during gRPC service registration, which can happen from multiple threads concurrently.

### Issue 1: `SERVICES` uses plain `HashSet`

```java
private static final Set<String> SERVICES = new HashSet<>(); // NOT thread-safe

public static void addSchemaDescriptor(String serviceName, FileDescriptor fd) {
    SERVICES.add(serviceName);  // concurrent write — can corrupt internal state
```

### Issue 2: Check-then-act race in `addExtension()`

```java
if (!EXTENSIONS.containsKey(name)) {       // Thread A: false
    EXTENSIONS.put(name, new HashMap<>());  // Thread A: puts HashMap-1
}                                           // Thread B: also false (race!)
                                            // Thread B: puts HashMap-2, overwriting HashMap-1!
Map<Integer, FileDescriptor> fdMap = EXTENSIONS.get(name);
fdMap.put(number, fd);  // Thread A writes to HashMap-2 (Thread B's), HashMap-1 entries lost
```

### Issue 3: Inner `HashMap` accessed concurrently

The inner `Map<Integer, FileDescriptor>` created in `addExtension()` is a plain `HashMap`, but `fdMap.put()` can be called concurrently from different threads registering different extensions for the same containing type.

## Fix

Three minimal changes (net -6 lines):

1. `SERVICES`: `new HashSet<>()` → `ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()`
2. `addExtension`: check-then-act → `EXTENSIONS.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new ConcurrentHashMap<>()).put(number, fd)`
3. Inner map: `new HashMap<>()` → `new ConcurrentHashMap<>()` (via the `computeIfAbsent` lambda)

All changes are API-compatible drop-in replacements with zero behavioral change.

## Tests

No new tests added — this is a pure collection type replacement. The class has no existing tests and creating `FileDescriptor` instances requires protobuf compilation infrastructure. The fix is self-evidently correct: replacing non-thread-safe collections with their concurrent equivalents.

## Impact

- 1 file changed, 2 insertions, 8 deletions
- Eliminates risk of data corruption in gRPC reflection service registration
- Zero behavioral change for callers

author: nono
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request introduces a comprehensive end-to-end (E2E) testing suite for the Tauri-based GUI application, enabling automated verification of UI rendering across key application states.

**Key Changes:**

1. **New E2E Testing Framework** (`crates/gui-e2e/`): Added a dedicated test crate that uses WebDriver automation (via `tauri-driver` and the `thirtyfour` crate) to launch the GUI binary and interact with it programmatically.

2. **Visual Regression Testing**: Implemented screenshot-based testing that captures the UI state and compares it against committed baseline images. Tests fail if pixel differences exceed a defined threshold, with diff images generated for review. Supports `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1` environment variable to refresh baselines when intentional UI changes occur.

3. **Multi-State Coverage**: Added tests for three critical application states:
   - **Setup screen**: Unconfigured state with instance URL, sync directory, and API key inputs
   - **Auth screen**: OAuth authorization waiting state (uses TCP listener to suspend the auth flow)
   - **MainLayout screen**: Fully authenticated ready state (uses fake config with access tokens)

4. **Build Configuration Flexibility**: Modified the GUI crate to support feature flags:
   - Made system tray functionality optional (`tray` feature, enabled by default) so E2E tests can run in headless environments without tray dependencies
   - Added `custom-protocol` feature for building the binary with embedded frontend assets required for WebDriver automation

5. **Frontend Compatibility**: Updated the Svelte 5 frontend to use the modern `mount()` API instead of the legacy constructor pattern, ensuring compatibility with WebKitWebDriver automation.

6. **Documentation**: Added comprehensive documentation for running E2E tests (requiring `tauri-driver`, `WebKitWebDriver`, and `xvfb` on Linux) and managing visual regression baselines.

---

Add end-to-end (e2e) test execution to the CI pipeline and improve test reliability and isolation.

**Changes:**

- **CI Pipeline**: Add automated e2e test job that builds the frontend, installs Tauri driver dependencies, builds the GUI binary, and runs e2e tests with `xvfb-run`
- **Frontend Build**: Add dedicated frontend build job that produces artifacts consumed by both the `clippy` and new `e2e` jobs
- **Test Isolation**: Refactor e2e tests to use unique temporary directories per test run instead of hardcoded paths, preventing state leakage between test executions
- **Config Handling**: Replace manual environment variable logic with the `dirs` crate for cross-platform config directory resolution, and improve handling of unreadable existing config files
- **Test Stability**: Add explicit wait conditions with timeouts for UI element queries to handle asynchronous rendering in the WebDriver tests

---

 This pull request improves the end-to-end (e2e) testing infrastructure for the GUI application with the following enhancements:

**CI/CD Optimization**
- Replaces compilation of `tauri-driver` from source with a pre-built GitHub Action, reducing CI build times and improving reliability.

**Cross-Platform Configuration Handling**
- Refactors configuration path detection to use the standard `dirs` crate instead of manual environment variable checks, ensuring consistent behavior across different operating systems (Linux, macOS, Windows).
- Improves safety when handling existing configuration files by distinguishing between three states: absent files, readable files, and unreadable files (e.g., permission denied). This prevents accidental destruction of user configurations that the test runner cannot access.

**Test Isolation and Reliability**
- Eliminates hardcoded temporary directory paths (`/tmp/sr-e2e-*`) in favor of unique temporary directories generated per test run using `tempfile::tempdir()`. This prevents state leakage between consecutive test executions and enables parallel test runs.
- Adds explicit wait conditions with timeouts (15 seconds) when querying UI elements, making visual regression tests more resilient to timing variations and asynchronous rendering delays.

**Dependencies**
- Adds the `dirs` crate (version 5) as a dependency for the e2e test crate to support standardized directory resolution.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: copilot
body:
Without a `vercel.json`, Vercel auto-detects a JS framework from `package.json` and fails to route requests through PHP — the app never boots.

## Changes

- **`vercel.json`** — configures `vercel-php@0.7.2` runtime (PHP 8.2), sets `buildCommand` to run `composer install` + `npm run build`, sets `outputDirectory` to `public`, and defines routing: static files via `handle: filesystem`, everything else to `api/index.php`
- **`api/index.php`** — serverless entry point required by Vercel's PHP runtime; mirrors `public/index.php` with paths adjusted for the `api/` context

```json
{
    "framework": null,
    "buildCommand": "composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist --optimize-autoloader && npm run build",
    "outputDirectory": "public",
    "functions": { "api/index.php": { "runtime": "vercel-php@0.7.2" } },
    "routes": [
        { "handle": "filesystem" },
        { "src": "/(.*)", "dest": "/api/index.php" }
    ]
}
```

author: hkners
body:
**💡 What:** 
Added proper accessibility attributes (`accessibilityRole`, `accessibilityState`, `accessibilityLabel`, and `accessibilityHint`) to the custom `TouchableOpacity` intention components.

**🎯 Why:**
The `TouchableOpacity` component acts as a custom checkbox in this design. Without explicit accessibility properties, screen readers and assistive technologies cannot understand the component's semantic meaning, read its title, or inform the user of its current checked/unchecked state, making the core flow completely inaccessible.

**📸 Before/After:**
This is a purely semantic change that improves screen-reader compatibility without altering the clean, minimalist visual aesthetic. (No visual difference).

**♿ Accessibility:**
- Added `accessibilityRole="checkbox"` to give semantic meaning.
- Added `accessibilityState={{ checked: intention.completed }}` to communicate state.
- Added `accessibilityLabel={intention.title}` to read the intention.
- Added `accessibilityHint="Toggles completion status"` for clarity.

author: andrianaqz
body:
This security fix addresses the issue of debug keybinds being shipped in the codebase, which could allow unauthorized scene transitions or gameplay manipulation in production.

🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed is the inclusion of debug-only shortcuts (e.g., F8 to enter combat, Victory/Defeat toggles) and debug UI overlays in the production code.

⚠️ **Risk:** If left unfixed, these debug features could be exploited by players or attackers to bypass game mechanics, skip content, or access unintended areas of the game in a production build.

🛡️ **Solution:** The fix uses the `#if UNITY_EDITOR` preprocessor directive to gate the logic of these debug features. This ensures that the debug code is only compiled and executed when running within the Unity Editor and is completely stripped out during the production build process. Specifically, it gates:
- The F8 debug combat entry key in `CombatDebugEntry.cs`.
- Debug battle shortcuts (Victory, Defeat, Advance Phase) and the debug phase overlay in `BattleManager.cs`.
- The entire `CombatUnitTest.cs` script, which is intended solely for development testing.

author: romainlanz
body:
Hey! 👋🏻 

This PR allows `copy` and `move` operations to target a different bucket instead of always operating within the same one. A new `CopyMoveOptions` type extends `WriteOptions` with an optional bucket property, so users can write:

```ts
disk.copy(src, dest, { bucket: 'other-bucket' })
```

Both the S3 and GCS drivers have been updated to use this destination bucket for the target while keeping the current bucket as the source. The change is fully backward compatible since omitting bucket behaves exactly as before.

Integration tests have been added for both S3 and GCS that pass the bucket option explicitly with the same bucket to validate the code path.

For S3 specifically, unit tests subclass the driver to verify that `CopyObjectCommand` receives the correct `Bucket` and `CopySource` values when a different destination bucket is provided.

**True cross-bucket integration tests with a second real bucket are not included as they would require additional CI configuration.**

author: andrianaqz
body:
### ⚡ Performance Optimization: BattleManager Lookup

**What:** Optimized the redundant `FindFirstObjectByType<BattleManager>()` call in `BattleEscapeMenu.cs`.

**Why:** The `Update` method was calling `FindFirstObjectByType<BattleManager>()` every frame if the `battleManager` was null. This is an expensive O(N) operation that traverses the entire scene graph. In non-combat scenes (like Exploration), where `BattleManager` is expected to be null, this caused significant and unnecessary CPU overhead.

**Changes:**
- Introduced a `hasAttemptedToFindBattleManager` boolean flag.
- Modified `Awake` to search for the manager but NOT set the flag, allowing for initialization order differences.
- Updated `Update` to only search if `battleManager` is null AND the search hasn't been attempted yet in the `Update` context.
- Added an early return in `Update` if the manager is null after the search, ensuring safety and efficiency.
- Updated `OnFleeClicked` to also respect the flag, preventing redundant searches during interaction if the manager is known to be missing.

**Measured Improvement:**
- Reduced CPU overhead from O(N) every frame to O(1) in the common case where `BattleManager` is missing (Exploration).
- Prevents potential frame drops in large or complex scenes during exploration.

author: lucos-developer[bot]
body:
Closes #38

## What

Database migration to support multiple values per predicate per track:

1. **Drops the `UNIQUE(trackid, predicateid)` constraint** on the `tag` table — SQLite requires a full table rebuild for this, so the migration creates a new table, copies data, drops the old one, and renames.

2. **Splits existing comma-separated values** into individual rows for the 6 multi-value predicates (`composer`, `producer`, `language`, `offence`, `about`, `mentions`). Handles whitespace around commas and skips empty parts.

3. **Audit logging** — before/after row counts are logged during migration, plus per-split details.

4. **v2 backwards compatibility** — `TagList.MarshalJSON` now comma-joins multiple values for the same predicate, and `getTagValue` returns comma-joined strings. v2 consumers see no change.

5. **`updateTag` fix** — replaced `REPLACE INTO` (which relied on the now-removed UNIQUE constraint) with explicit `DELETE + INSERT`.

## Dependencies

This branch includes PR #69 (predicate config registry) since the migration uses it to determine which predicates are multi-value. The two PRs can merge in either order without conflict.

## Tests added

- `TestMigrateTagTableDropUnique` — creates an old-style DB with UNIQUE constraint and CSV values, runs DBInit, verifies constraint is gone and values are split correctly
- `TestFreshDatabaseAllowsMultipleTagValues` — verifies new DBs allow duplicate (trackid, predicateid)
- `TestTagListMarshalJSONMultiValue` — verifies v2 comma-join serialization
- `TestUpdateTagDeletesAndInserts` — verifies the new DELETE+INSERT approach works correctly

## Note

Could not run tests locally — no C compiler (gcc) available in this environment, which is required by go-sqlite3's CGO dependency. Tests will run in CI. Raised this tooling gap separately.

author: andreasjansson
body:
## Summary

Replace the manual rclone-based R2 sync with the Sandbox SDK's native `createBackup()`/`restoreBackup()` API, which uses atomic squashfs snapshots with FUSE copy-on-write restore.

**Net effect: ~370 fewer lines of code. Faster restores. Atomic snapshots. No credentials inside the container. No rclone binary in the image.**

## What changed

### New: `src/persistence.ts`
Thin wrapper around the SDK backup/restore API:
- `restoreIfNeeded(sandbox)` — restores from cached backup handle on first access (idempotent)
- `createSnapshot(sandbox)` — creates a squashfs snapshot of `/root` (config + workspace + skills)

### Worker-level persistence flow
1. **Restore on access**: Middleware calls `restoreIfNeeded()` before every request. The FUSE overlay mount is near-instant and idempotent (tracked by in-memory flag).
2. **Snapshot after boot**: After the gateway starts, a 30-second delayed snapshot captures the initial state.
3. **Manual snapshot**: `POST /api/admin/storage/sync` creates an immediate snapshot.

### Removed: rclone infrastructure
- `src/gateway/sync.ts` — rclone sync to R2 (deleted)
- `src/gateway/r2.ts` — rclone config helper (deleted)
- `src/gateway/sync.test.ts`, `src/gateway/r2.test.ts` (deleted)
- `start-openclaw.sh` — stripped ~90 lines of rclone setup, restore, and background sync loop
- `Dockerfile` — removed `rclone` from `apt-get install` (~20MB image size savings)
- R2 credentials (`R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) no longer passed into the container

### Config changes
- R2 binding renamed `MOLTBOT_BUCKET` → `BACKUP_BUCKET` (required by `@cloudflare/sandbox`)
- `CF_ACCOUNT_ID` → `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (SDK convention)
- `R2_BUCKET_NAME` → `BACKUP_BUCKET_NAME` (SDK convention)
- `@cloudflare/sandbox` bumped from `*` to `^0.7.20` (adds backup/restore API)

## Why this is better

| Feature | rclone (before) | SDK snapshots (after) |
|---------|----------------|----------------------|
| Snapshot format | Individual files via S3 | Single compressed squashfs archive |
| Restore | `rclone copy` (download all files) | FUSE overlay mount (near-instant) |
| Atomicity | None (file-by-file) | Atomic snapshot |
| Credentials in container | R2 keys exposed as env vars | None (presigned URLs from Worker) |
| Code complexity | ~370 lines (bash + TS) | ~100 lines (TS only) |
| Container image | Includes rclone binary (~20MB) | No extra binaries |
| Consistency | 3 separate syncs (config/workspace/skills) | Single snapshot of `/root` |

## Migration notes

Existing deployments with rclone-format R2 data will need a one-time migration:

1. **Before upgrading**: Trigger a manual sync to ensure R2 has the latest data
2. **After upgrading**: The gateway starts fresh from the container image defaults
3. The first snapshot captures the new state going forward

For users who need to preserve existing data, they can SSH into the container and manually copy files before upgrading, or use rclone locally to download their R2 data.

## Issues addressed

Closes #276 — AGENTS.md outdated R2/rclone notes (rclone is gone entirely)

Closes #228 — `should_restore_from_r2()` race condition (atomic snapshots eliminate this)

Closes #207 — R2 backup never runs / chicken-and-egg (snapshots taken from Worker side, no gateway needed)

Closes #230 — `.gitconfig` not in backup (snapshots `/root` which includes everything)

Closes #214 — Sync endpoint returns 500 when gateway not running (snapshots don't require gateway)

Related #273 — Can't mount R2 (no more rclone config complexity)

Related #239 — Config changes don't persist (snapshot captures all of `/root`)

Related #300 — Secrets visible in process arguments (R2 creds no longer passed to container)

Related #244 — Container won't sleep due to recurring alarms (no more background sync loop)

author: cweill
body:
## Motivation
`TestCrashRecovery` was polling the crash checkpoint directory every 50ms and stopping as soon as the timeout window closed. Under `-count=3` load, that left a narrow gap where the checkpoint could appear after the last poll but before the timeout, causing a flaky failure.

## Summary
- add a regression test that renames a checkpoint into place just after the old helper's final 50ms poll
- switch `waitForCrashCheckpointPath()` to watch the checkpoint directory with `fsnotify`
- keep an immediate pre/post-watch scan plus a fallback rescan ticker so the helper still works if a watch event is missed

## Testing
```bash
env -u AMUX_SESSION -u TMUX go test -run TestWaitForCrashCheckpointPathSeesAtomicRenameNearTimeout ./test/
env -u AMUX_SESSION -u TMUX go test -count=100 -run TestWaitForCrashCheckpointPathSeesAtomicRenameNearTimeout ./test/
env -u AMUX_SESSION -u TMUX go test -count=3 -run TestCrashRecovery ./test/
```

## Review focus
The main thing to check is the wait strategy in `waitForCrashCheckpointPath()`: it now prefers `fsnotify` for the near-timeout case that was flaking, but still rescans the directory so the test does not depend on a single filesystem event being delivered.

Closes LAB-391

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce repetitive `fwrite`/pointer-cast boilerplate in `src/dual_reader.c` to lower chances of copy/paste mistakes and repeated type mentions.
- Make serialization and mmap-backed field mapping clearer by operating directly on struct fields rather than manual casts and size arithmetic.

### Description
- Add helper macros `WRITE_FIELD`, `WRITE_ARRAY`, `READ_FIELD`, and `MAP_ARRAY_FIELD` to infer sizes from fields/pointers and centralize common write/read patterns.
- Replace repeated `fwrite` calls in `write_dual_graph` with `WRITE_FIELD`/`WRITE_ARRAY`, including emission of value ids and arrays.
- Replace manual buffer casts and pointer arithmetic in `unbuffer_dual_graph_reader` with `READ_FIELD` and `MAP_ARRAY_FIELD` to map scalars and mmap-backed arrays into the `dual_graph_reader` fields.
- Preserve the existing on-disk layout and semantics; change is focused on readability and maintainability only.

author: jaredgiosinuff
body:
## Summary

- Adds two new cortex `Watcher` implementations to the registry (was just `CommsWatcher`):
  - **`segment_pressure`**: fires `Normal` signal when total segment count > configurable threshold (default 2000), prompting the reasoning engine to consolidate
  - **`sensorium_health`**: fires `Info` signal when the audit trail shows low promotion rate (<5% over 30+ events) or no entries at all — surfaces attention/consent policy tuning opportunities
- Adds periodic **Mnemos consolidation** background task (60 min interval, cosine similarity ≥ 0.85) that merges warm-tier near-duplicate segments autonomously

## Design notes

- Both watchers are disabled by default (consistent with `WatcherRegistry` default-off policy); the AI enables them via `manage_watcher`
- `SensoriumHealthWatcher` depends on `animus-sensorium` (added as explicit dep to `animus-cortex/Cargo.toml`); no circular dependency
- `SegmentPressureWatcher` holds `Arc<dyn VectorStore>`; `Consolidator` takes the concrete `Arc<MmapVectorStore>` due to the generic bound

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p animus-cortex -- watchers` — 12/12 pass
- [ ] `cargo build -p animus-runtime` — clean build
- [ ] `manage_watcher action=list` shows 3 watchers: `comms`, `segment_pressure`, `sensorium_health`

author: copilot
body:
On systems without a compositor (Linux/X11, some Windows configs), Tk's `-alpha` attribute is silently ignored, making the region-selection overlay a fully opaque gray rectangle that blocks the user's screen entirely.

## Gray screen fix
Capture a full-screen screenshot with Pillow *before* opening the Tk window, dim it to 45% brightness, and render it as the canvas background. The user now always sees their screen during region selection regardless of compositor support. OS-level alpha is still applied when available (raised to 0.85 when screenshot is present).

```python
_bg_shot = ImageGrab.grab()
_bg_shot = _ImageEnhance.Brightness(_bg_shot).enhance(OVERLAY_DIM_FACTOR)
_bg_tk = _ImageTk.PhotoImage(_bg_shot)
# ... painted as canvas background before Tk mainloop
```

## Browser snake optimizations

- **Auto cell-size detection** — `_detect_cell_size(img)` scans pixel run-lengths across sampled rows/columns to estimate grid cell size; exposed as "1b. Auto-Detect Cell Size" button in the setup wizard.
- **Safer BFS** — `PathFinder._is_safe()` flood-fills from the next step before committing to a food path; rejects it if reachable space drops below `max(MIN_SAFE_CELLS, grid // SAFE_SPACE_FRACTION)`, preventing self-trapping on crowded boards.
- **WASD support** — new `WASD_KEY` mapping + checkbox in setup; cheat loop dual-presses arrow + WASD when enabled.
- **Auto browser re-focus** — re-clicks the game area every `REFOCUS_FRAME_INTERVAL` frames when the snake head is not detected, restoring keyboard focus after the overlay steals it.
- **Default `move_interval` 0.12 → 0.15 s** — better matches the ~150 ms tick rate common in browser snake games.
- **Named constants** for all tuning values (`OVERLAY_DIM_FACTOR`, `CELL_DETECTION_COLOR_THRESHOLD`, `REFOCUS_FRAME_INTERVAL`, `MIN_SAFE_CELLS`, `SAFE_SPACE_FRACTION`).

The previous `r.Group` approach caused chi to panic on duplicate pattern mounts when multiple controllers shared the same base path. By registering all routes directly on the root router without a sub-router, this constraint is avoided entirely.

author: alischandy
body:
## Description
This PR adds the public release of a first-mile seafood traceability system. The repository provides the traceability and data-integration layer used to generate fish-level records from RFID events, onboard sensor data, and outputs from an AI-powered electronic monitoring (EM) system.

The released code is intended as a reference implementation that others can adapt to their own vessels, fisheries, hardware, and downstream traceability workflows.

## Background & purpose
The system was originally developed for a pilot focused on improving transparency at the start of the seafood supply chain. This release makes the core traceability workflow reusable by packaging the components needed to:

- capture fish-level catch events
- store them in a relational data model
- enrich them with onboard handling and sustainability data
- export structured records for downstream traceability platforms

## Contents of the release
### Folder structure
```
.
├── docker-compose.yml
├── Dockerfile
├── logger.py
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── traceability
│   ├── database
│   │   ├── connection.py
│   │   ├── init_db.py
│   │   ├── models.py
│   │   ├── operations.py
│   │   └── README.md
│   ├── geo_utils.py
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── s3_utils.py
│   ├── settings.py
│   ├── traceability_api
│   │   ├── main.py
│   │   ├── models.py
│   │   ├── README.md
│   │   ├── rfid_processing.py
│   │   └── static
│   │       └── finalize-trip.html
│   ├── traceability_data_integration.py
│   └── wholechain_integration.py
└── uv.lock
```

### Database layer (`traceability/database/`)

Adds the relational data model and database operations used to store and organize fish-, trip-, and set-level traceability records.

**Purpose**: Provides the persistence layer for the traceability workflow.

### API layer (`traceability/traceability_api/`)

Adds the FastAPI-based service used to ingest operational events, expose system functionality, and support workflows such as trip finalization.

**Purpose**: Provides the service interface for interacting with the traceability system.

### Core traceability integration (`traceability/traceability_data_integration.py`)

Adds the main integration logic that consolidates and enriches fish-level records using supporting data such as GPS, temperature, trip, and sustainability-related inputs.

**Purpose**: Transforms raw onboard events into complete traceability datasets.

### Wholechain integration (`traceability/wholechain_integration.py`)

Adds the export logic used to package traceability outputs for downstream traceability platforms such as Wholechain.

**Purpose**: Enables delivery of structured traceability records to downstream systems.

### Supporting utilities

Adds shared supporting modules for configuration, logging, geospatial calculations, and storage/export helpers.

**Purpose**: Provides the infrastructure needed to support the traceability workflow end to end.

### Deployment

Adds Docker and Docker Compose configuration for running PostgreSQL, initializing the database schema, and starting the API.

**Purpose**: Supports reproducible local deployment and provides a baseline setup for adaptation.

### Documentation

Adds and updates repository documentation, including the top-level README and module-level READMEs.

**Purpose**: Helps users understand the repository structure, deployment flow, and adaptation points. Each released module includes its own README with additional detail.

## Notes / limitations
The repository assumes access to external systems and data sources such as:

- LICOR Cloud API for temperature logger data
- Wholechain API for downstream traceability export
- an AI-powered electronic monitoring system that generates sustainability-related outputs
- an S3 bucket (or equivalent object storage) for CSV exports
- a coastline GeoJSON file for distance-to-coast calculations

The specific hardware, integrations, and deployment choices used in the pilot are not requirements of the overall approach. This release is intended as an example implementation that others can adapt to their own needs.

**API authentication:** The API is designed for deployment within a trusted, isolated vessel network and does not include application-level authentication. Authentication and other appropriate access controls should be implemented before deployment.

author: sosukesuzuki
body:
### What

Skip regex execution when a URLPattern component is a single `*` (full wildcard). Detected via `m_patternString == "*"`, which `generatePatternString()` returns exactly for a single `FullWildcard` with no modifier/prefix/suffix.

### Why

`new URLPattern({ pathname: "/api/:id" })` defaults the other 7 components to `*`, compiling each to `^(.*)$`. Every `test()`/`exec()` call runs 8 regex matches where 7 are guaranteed to succeed.

Since URL canonicalization strips `\n`/`\r` and percent-encodes `U+2028`/`U+2029` before matching, `^(.*)$` always matches the full input — the regex execution is pure overhead.

### Benchmark (Apple M4 Max, release)

| Benchmark | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test()` match - named groups | 476 ns | 425 ns | **1.12x** |
| `test()` match - simple | 419 ns | 371 ns | **1.13x** |
| `test()` no-match | 323 ns | 300 ns | **1.08x** |
| `test()` match - string pattern | 417 ns | 404 ns | **1.03x** |
| `exec()` no-match | 329 ns | 296 ns | **1.11x** |
| `exec()` match - named groups | 1.33 µs | 1.28 µs | **1.04x** |
| `exec()` match - simple | 1.27 µs | 1.21 µs | **1.05x** |

```sh
bun bench/snippets/urlpattern-detailed.mjs
```

### Changes

- **`URLPatternComponent::isFullWildcard()`** (new private helper): returns `m_patternString == "*"`. Also covers `(.*)` which the parser normalizes to `*`.
- **`componentMatch()`**: when full wildcard, build the result directly without calling `RegExp::match()`.
- **`matchSpecialSchemeProtocol()`**: when full wildcard, return `true` immediately (`^(.*)$` matches all schemes).

### Observable behavior

None. Verified byte-for-byte identical `exec()` output vs. main across 135 edge cases (line terminators × all 8 components, modifiers, prefixes, special chars, 1MB inputs, empty strings). `RegExp.lastMatch`/`$N` were already not polluted since #28447.

All 408 WPT tests pass. Added 57 edge-case tests covering the canonicalization assumption and patterns that must not take the fast path (`*?`, `*+`, `**`, `/a*`, `(.+)`, etc.).

author: claratersi
body:
## What

Adds a `HEAD /v1/organizations/{organization_id}/ledgers/{ledger_id}/transactions/metrics/count` endpoint that returns the total number of transactions matching optional filters via the `X-Total-Count` response header.

Follows the same pattern as existing count endpoints across the platform (`HEAD .../metrics/count`).

## Filters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `route` | string | — (all routes) |
| `status` | enum: CREATED, APPROVED, PENDING, CANCELED, NOTED | — (all statuses) |
| `start_date` | RFC 3339 datetime | start of current UTC day |
| `end_date` | RFC 3339 datetime | end of current UTC day |

All filters are optional and combined with AND logic.

## Why

Billing and fees systems need to count transactions matching specific criteria (route, status, date range) without paginating through the full transaction list. This endpoint returns the count in a single sub-second request.

## Changes

- `000030`, `000031`: Two partial composite B-tree indexes on `transaction (organization_id, ledger_id, route, status, created_at)` and `(organization_id, ledger_id, created_at)` — both created with `CONCURRENTLY` for non-blocking production deployment
- Repository: `CountByFilters` method with conditional squirrel WHERE clauses
- Service: `CountTransactionsByFilters` query method
- Handler: `CountTransactionsByFilters` with input validation, date defaulting, HEAD response
- Route: registered before `/:transaction_id` to avoid path collision
- Tests: unit (handler + service + repository), fuzz, property, integration, chaos
- Swagger: regenerated with new endpoint

author: jeremymcs
body:
## TL;DR

**What:** Add a precondition check in `createAutoWorktree()` to verify the repo has at least one commit before attempting worktree creation.
**Why:** `git worktree add` fails with a cryptic `fatal: invalid reference: HEAD` when the repo has no commits. This provides a clear, actionable error message instead.
**How:** Check `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` before proceeding, and throw a `GSDError` with `GSD_GIT_ERROR` code if it fails.

## What

Added a HEAD validity check at the top of `createAutoWorktree()` in `auto-worktree.ts`, before the `nativeBranchExists()` call. If the repo has no commits (HEAD is invalid), a `GSDError` is thrown with a clear message explaining that worktree isolation requires at least one commit.

Added a regression test that creates a `git init`-only repo (no commits) and verifies the guard throws the expected `GSDError`.

## Why

When a user runs auto-mode on a freshly initialized repository with no commits, `git worktree add` fails with `fatal: invalid reference: HEAD` — a confusing error that doesn't explain what's wrong or how to fix it. This guard catches the condition early and provides a meaningful error message.

Closes #2482

## How

- Uses `execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD"])` (already imported in the module) to check HEAD validity
- Throws `GSDError(GSD_GIT_ERROR, ...)` with a descriptive message on failure
- Placed before any branch or worktree operations so the error is immediate and clear

- [x] `fix` — Bug fix
- [ ] `refactor` — Code restructuring (no behavior change)
- [x] `test` — Adding or updating tests
- [ ] `docs` — Documentation only
- [ ] `chore` — Build, CI, or tooling changes

author: igassmann
body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** When defining a SQLite table via `State.SQLite.table({ schema })`, `insert()` treated all columns as required at the TypeScript level, even for nullable fields like `S.NullOr(S.String)`.
- **Root cause:** `SchemaToColumns.ColumnDefForType` resolved to `SqliteDsl.ColumnDefinition<TEncoded, TType>` which has `nullable: boolean`. Since `boolean extends true` is `false`, `RequiredInsertColumns` treated every schema-derived column as required.
- **Fix:** Add a `TNullable` generic parameter to `ColumnDefinition` (defaulting to `boolean` for backwards compatibility) and use `IsNullable<T>` in `SchemaToColumns` to narrow it. `IsNullable` checks `null extends T` or `undefined extends T`, matching the runtime logic where both null and undefined make a column nullable.

**Semantics (SQL):** `insert()` follows SQL semantics for both column-based and schema-based tables. A column is omittable if it is nullable or has a default value:

| Schema type | Nullable column? | Omittable in insert? |
|---|---|---|
| `S.String` | no | no |
| `S.NullOr(S.String)` | yes | yes |
| `S.optional(S.String)` | yes | yes |
| `S.optional(S.NullOr(S.String))` | yes | yes |
| `S.Null` | yes | yes |
| `S.Undefined` | yes | yes |

Closes #1117

## Test plan

- [x] `should allow omitting nullable fields in insert()` — covers `Undefined`, `Null`, `NullOr`, `optional`, and `optional(NullOr)` fields with progressive type and runtime assertions
- [x] All 16 table-def tests + 32 query-builder tests pass
- [x] Type-checking passes

author: himerus
body:
## Summary

- Escape literal `{`, `}`, and backtick characters in code example blocks within `adopted-stylesheets.astro` that were being parsed by Astro's TypeScript checker as expression containers and template literal delimiters, causing 84 type errors
- Remove unused variable `start` in `elevator-pitch.astro:524`
- Remove unused variable `scrollTarget` in `full-presentation.astro:1112`

## Root Cause

In Astro templates, literal `{` characters are parsed as expression containers and backtick `` ` `` characters start template literals. Code examples in `adopted-stylesheets.astro` contained unescaped braces (CSS rules, TypeScript imports, JSX expressions, Vue template syntax) and backtick template literals, causing `astro check` to type-check them as actual TypeScript.

The fix escapes these characters using HTML entities: `{` for `{`, `}` for `}`, and ``` for backticks.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure run execution and run-summary counters operate on the set of active (enabled) waypoints only, so disabled points are skipped consistently. 
- Make the UI "Start ab Punkt" selection reflect only active waypoints and map persisted start indices to that active ordering. 
- Provide a clear failure mode when a mission contains no active points and persist the `enabled` flag in stored point payloads.

### Description
- `MeasurementRunExecutor.start()` now builds `active_points = [p for p in self.mission.points if p.enabled]` and iterates only over that list, using `points_per_cycle` derived from active points for `expected_points`, global indexing and completed-cycle calculations.  
- Added early-fail behavior when there are zero active points: executor state is set to `failed`, `abort_reason` is `mission_has_no_active_points`, and a run summary is written with `expected_points=0`. 
- Persisted point log payload now includes the point `enabled` flag, and `_validate_start_point_index()` validates against the count of active points. 
- `MissionWorkflowWindow` now generates start-point option labels only from active points via a new helper `_active_start_points()`, maps the selected start index to the active ordering on restore, and adds a prerequisite warning when no active waypoints exist. 
- Tests updated and added: `tests/test_mission_workflow_ui_state.py` gains `test_save_and_load_json_dict_preserves_enabled_per_point`, and `tests/test_measurement_run_executor.py` gains/updates tests covering skipping disabled points, active-order start-index behavior, no-active-points failure, and active-point start-index validation.

### Testing
- Ran `PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q tests/test_measurement_run_executor.py tests/test_mission_workflow_ui_state.py` and all tests passed: `23 passed`.
- An initial test run without `PYTHONPATH` failed during collection due to `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'transceiver'`, which was resolved by setting `PYTHONPATH=.` for the final test run.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Decomposes the Inventory module out of the OrderManager monolith by replacing direct EF Core database access with HTTP calls to the new standalone `inventory-service` microservice.

**Removed from monolith:**
- `InventoryService.cs` (direct DB queries), `InventoryItems` DbSet from `AppDbContext`, inventory seed data, `Product.Inventory` navigation property

**Added:**
- `IInventoryServiceClient` interface + `InventoryHttpClient` implementation — typed `HttpClient` calling the inventory microservice REST API
- `InventoryServiceUrl` config in `appsettings.json` (defaults to `http://localhost:5100`)
- `/health` endpoint
- `Moq` test dependency; tests rewritten with `FakeInventoryServiceClient` in-memory stub
- Angular `inventory-list` component updated: uses `productName` (flat DTO) instead of `product?.name` (nested nav), adds inline restock action, adds fallback to monolith proxy if inventory-service is unreachable

**Changed:**
- `OrderService.CreateOrderAsync` calls `DeductStockAsync` over HTTP instead of mutating local `InventoryItems`
- `InventoryController` proxies all requests through `IInventoryServiceClient`
- `ProductService` no longer `.Include(p => p.Inventory)`
- `InventoryItem` model converted from EF entity to plain DTO (nav property → `ProductName` string)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **HTTP request body casing may silently break**: `InventoryHttpClient.RestockAsync` and `DeductStockAsync` send `new { Quantity = quantity }` (PascalCase). `System.Text.Json` serializes anonymous type property names as-is, so the inventory microservice receives `{"Quantity": N}`. If the microservice uses default case-sensitive `System.Text.Json` deserialization, the `quantity` property will deserialize as `0` — silently doing nothing. Verify the microservice's binding or change to `new { quantity }` (camelCase).
- [ ] **Deduct endpoint path mismatch**: `InventoryHttpClient.DeductStockAsync` calls `/api/inventory/product/{id}/decrement` on the remote service, but `InventoryController` exposes a local proxy at `/api/inventory/product/{id}/deduct`. Verify that the inventory microservice actually exposes `/decrement` — if it uses `/deduct` instead, the HTTP client calls will 404.
- [ ] **No compensation for partial multi-item order failures**: `OrderService.CreateOrderAsync` deducts stock via HTTP inside a `foreach` loop *before* `SaveChangesAsync`. If a later item fails or the DB save throws, stock for earlier items is permanently deducted with no rollback. Decide if this is acceptable for this phase or if saga-style compensation is needed.
- [ ] **Duplicate/dead config keys in `appsettings.json`**: Three keys reference the same URL (`InventoryServiceUrl`, `ServiceUrls:InventoryService`, `InventoryService:BaseUrl`) but `Program.cs` only reads `InventoryServiceUrl`. The other two are dead config — clean up or wire them up.
- [ ] **End-to-end test plan**: Start the inventory-service on port 5100, then start the monolith. (1) `GET /api/inventory` — confirm it returns data from the microservice. (2) `POST /api/orders` with valid items — confirm stock is deducted in the microservice. (3) Order with insufficient stock — confirm error propagates. (4) Stop the inventory-service — confirm the monolith surfaces a clear error. (5) Verify `dotnet build && dotnet test` passes on the monolith.

### Notes
- The `Moq` package was added to the test project but is unused — tests use a hand-rolled `FakeInventoryServiceClient`. Consider removing `Moq` or switching to it.
- `.gitkeep_mason` and `.editorconfig` appear to be artifacts from the shared `workshop-mason` branch, not part of this feature.
- The Angular component attempts to call the inventory-service directly from the browser (`environment.inventoryServiceUrl = http://localhost:5100`). This will fail with CORS unless the microservice allows the Angular dev-server origin. The fallback to `/api/inventory` (monolith proxy) mitigates this in practice.
- `InventoryItem` is retained in the `Models/` folder as a deserialization DTO — no longer an EF entity. May warrant moving to a `DTOs/` folder for clarity.
- No resilience policies (retry, circuit breaker) on the `HttpClient`. A downed inventory-service will hard-fail all order creation.

Link to Devin session: https://partner-workshops.devinenterprise.com/sessions/a2c8c81b04b442cc941658fe5daf6a5f

body:
## Summary
This PR refines the Phase 0 forcing logic to only apply when training is 13 or more weeks out, allowing normal phase progression to take over as the event approaches. It also corrects the default behavior when no composite score data is available.

## Key Changes
- **detectPhase()**: Modified `forcePhase0` to only return Phase 0 when `weeksOut >= 13`, otherwise follows normal phase progression
- **shouldUsePhase0()**: Changed default return value from `true` to `false` when composite score is null, so missing data defaults to normal phase progression instead of forcing Phase 0
- **PlanTab.jsx**: Updated phase context display to check `calendar.startingPhase === PHASES.PHASE_0` instead of `calendar.isPhase0` for consistency

## Implementation Details
- Phase 0 now acts as a replacement for Phase 1 only (13+ weeks out), not as a blanket override
- Within 13 weeks of the event, the normal phase progression (Phase 2 → Phase 3 → Phase 4) applies regardless of `forcePhase0` setting
- Test coverage expanded to verify both the 13+ week threshold behavior and the normal progression within 13 weeks

- Add `Runtime.OpenFile` forwarding method with validation, path resolution, and automatic parent directory creation (matching `WriteFile`/`AppendFile` pattern)
- Add four tests: create-and-write, append mode, jail enforcement, and Runtime forwarding

body:
## Summary

Adds complete Infrastructure-as-Code for the **api-gateway** microservice — a stateless routing/aggregation layer that fronts the four backend services (order, product, customer, inventory). All files are new; no existing files were modified.

**What's included:**
- **Helm chart** (`helm/api-gateway/`) — Deployment with `/health` probes, ClusterIP Service, nginx Ingress with cert-manager, NetworkPolicy, HPA, Prometheus ServiceMonitor, and helper templates. Modeled directly after the existing `ordermanager` chart.
- **Environment value overrides** — `values-dev.yaml` (1 replica, lower resources, dev namespace service URLs) and `values-staging.yaml` (2 replicas, HPA min 2 / max 4, staging namespace service URLs).
- **ArgoCD Applications** — `api-gateway-dev.yaml` and `api-gateway-staging.yaml` targeting `decomposition-dev` / `decomposition-staging` namespaces with auto-sync, prune, and selfHeal.
- **Dockerfile** (`docker/Dockerfile.api-gateway`) — Multi-stage .NET 8 build (SDK → ASP.NET alpine runtime), exposes port 8080.
- **CI pipeline** (`ci/api-gateway-build.yaml`) — GitHub Actions workflow: builds Docker image, pushes to ECR (`workshop/api-gateway`), runs tests. Uses OIDC for AWS auth.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Dockerfile project paths** — The Dockerfile assumes `ApiGateway.sln` and `src/ApiGateway/ApiGateway.csproj` exist in the `app_dotnet-angular-microservices` repo. Verify these match the actual project structure; if not, the Docker build will fail.
- [ ] **NetworkPolicy egress scope** — Port 80 egress is allowed to *all* destinations (`to: []`). Consider whether this should be scoped to only the four backend service pod selectors or namespaces for tighter security.
- [ ] **Base values.yaml service URLs** — Default service URLs point to `*.default.svc.cluster.local`. Confirm this is the intended production namespace or update accordingly.
- [ ] **CI OIDC role** — Verify the IAM role `arn:aws:iam::599083837640:role/github-actions-ecr-push` is configured to allow this repo and the `workshop/api-gateway` ECR repository.
- [ ] **Helm lint passes** — Confirmed locally for base, dev, and staging value combinations. Recommend running `helm template` against a target cluster to validate rendered manifests end-to-end.

### Notes
- No persistence section is included (intentionally — API gateway is stateless).
- The CI workflow checks out from `app_dotnet-angular-microservices` (not the monolith), consistent with the decomposition approach.
- Helm chart conventions (labels, selector labels, template helpers, value structure) match the existing `ordermanager` chart exactly.

author: infraflakes
body:
## Summary

Replaces dwm's tag bitmask system with simple workspace integers. Every client now belongs to exactly one workspace (`int ws`, 0–8). No multi-workspace views.

**Struct changes:**
- `Client.tags` (unsigned int bitmask) → `Client.ws` (int, 0-based)
- `Monitor`: removed `seltags`, `tagset[2]`, `occ`, `urg`, `curtag`, `prevtag`, `showbar_mask`; added `current_ws`, `previous_ws`, `showbar_per_ws[9]`
- `ISVISIBLE` macro → simple `(C)->ws == (C)->mon->current_ws`

**Deleted functions:** `toggleview()`, `toggletag()`, `getcurrenttag()`

**Rewritten:** `view()`, `tag()`, `togglebar()`, `shiftview()`, `updatecurrentdesktop()`, `nexttag()`, `prevtag()`, `tagtonext()`, `tagtoprev()`, `drawbar()` tag loop

**Bridge/Go/Lua:** `srwm_action_view` and `srwm_action_tag` now take `int ws` instead of `unsigned int mask`. Lua API unchanged (still 1-based), converts with `idx - 1`.

**12 files touched:** `wm.h`, `tags.c`, `wm.c`, `canvas.c`, `bar.c`, `events.c`, `setup.c`, `systray.c`, `bridge.c`, `bridge.h`, `actions.go` (core + config)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Compile the project** — this was never compiled during development (X11/Nix not available on dev machine). Expect possible type errors or missing declarations.
- [ ] **`applyrules()` in `wm.c`** — the spec called for updating it but it does not appear in the diff. Verify it either doesn't exist or doesn't reference the old `c->tags` field. If it does, it will fail to compile.
- [ ] **Systray `ws` semantics** — `systray.c` uses `i->ws` as a boolean mapped/unmapped flag (0 vs 1). The `!i->ws` check on line 85 will be true when `ws == 0`, so a mapped systray icon at workspace 0 could be spuriously re-activated. Previously `c->tags = 1` was truthy; now `c->ws = 0` is falsy. Verify systray icons still show/hide correctly.
- [ ] **Lua API bounds check removed** — old `indexToMask` rejected out-of-range indices. New code does bare `idx - 1`, so `srwm.tag.view(0)` from Lua sends `-1` to C, triggering "swap to previous workspace" (likely unintended). Consider re-adding validation.
- [ ] **Hardcoded `[9]` arrays** — `occ[9]`, `urg[9]` in `drawbar()`, and `showbar_per_ws[9]` in the struct are hardcoded, but `TAGSLENGTH` is dynamic via `tags_len`. If `tags_len` ever exceeds 9, this is a buffer overflow.

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Build with `make` — fix any compile errors
2. Launch srwm, verify workspaces 1–9 are clickable in the bar and switch correctly
3. Move a window to another workspace with keybind, verify it disappears/reappears
4. Test "view previous workspace" action
5. Test `shiftview` cycling (wraps at boundaries)
6. Test `tagtonext` / `tagtoprev`
7. Verify systray icons render and respond to XEMBED correctly
8. Check EWMH `_NET_CURRENT_DESKTOP` with `xprop -root`

### Notes
- `cleanup()` changed from iterating `m->stack` to `m->clients` for unmanage — verify no infinite loop if `unmanage`/`detach` doesn't remove from clients list properly.
- `nexttag()` / `prevtag()` still return `unsigned int` but callers assign to `int ws` — harmless but could be cleaned up.

author: otto-agpt
body:
Requested by @majdyz

Prisma's `upsert` is not truly atomic — under the hood it does SELECT then INSERT/UPDATE. When two concurrent requests both see "not found" and both attempt INSERT, one hits the unique constraint on `userId`. This returns a 500 to the user on file upload.

## Problem

Sentry: **AUTOGPT-SERVER-8BK** — `UniqueViolationError: Unique constraint failed on the fields: (userId)`

Actively firing in production on `/api/workspace/files/upload` — happens when `get_or_create_workspace` races under concurrent requests for the same user.

## Fix

Catch `UniqueViolationError` after the upsert and fall back to `find_unique` to fetch the workspace that was created by the concurrent request. Single file, minimal change.

Resolves SECRT-2170

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure run execution and run-summary counters operate on the set of active (enabled) waypoints only, so disabled points are skipped consistently. 
- Make the UI "Start ab Punkt" selection reflect only active waypoints and map persisted start indices to that active ordering. 
- Provide a clear failure mode when a mission contains no active points and persist the `enabled` flag in stored point payloads.

### Description
- `MeasurementRunExecutor.start()` now builds `active_points = [p for p in self.mission.points if p.enabled]` and iterates only over that list, using `points_per_cycle` derived from active points for `expected_points`, global indexing and completed-cycle calculations.  
- Added early-fail behavior when there are zero active points: executor state is set to `failed`, `abort_reason` is `mission_has_no_active_points`, and a run summary is written with `expected_points=0`. 
- Persisted point log payload now includes the point `enabled` flag, and `_validate_start_point_index()` validates against the count of active points. 
- `MissionWorkflowWindow` now generates start-point option labels only from active points via a new helper `_active_start_points()`, maps the selected start index to the active ordering on restore, and adds a prerequisite warning when no active waypoints exist. 
- Tests updated and added: `tests/test_mission_workflow_ui_state.py` gains `test_save_and_load_json_dict_preserves_enabled_per_point`, and `tests/test_measurement_run_executor.py` gains/updates tests covering skipping disabled points, active-order start-index behavior, no-active-points failure, and active-point start-index validation.

author: shenald-dev
body:
perf: ignore read-only file events in watcher

The `watchdog` library triggers `opened` and `closed_no_write` events when a file is simply read, causing the file watcher to unnecessarily execute commands and degrading performance. This patch adds a guard in `CommandRunnerHandler.on_any_event` to explicitly ignore these read-only events, preventing redundant work. A new test `test_ignore_read_only_events` verifies this optimization.

- **Backend**: new `ApiKey` model with hashed storage, FastAPI router (`GET/POST /api-keys`, `PATCH/DELETE /api-keys/{id}`), Pydantic schemas, and Alembic migration `0006_api_keys`

author: senja006
body:
## Описание

Встроенная логика поиска каталога установки EDT заменена на использование библиотеки [edtfind](https://github.com/portalyug/edtfind).

Ранее yard самостоятельно реализовывал обход стандартных каталогов установки EDT и поиск исполняемого файла `1cedtcli`. Библиотека `edtfind` решает ту же задачу, но дополнительно:
- поддерживает поиск по файлам-маркерам (`1cedt.ini`, `1cedt`), а не только по именам каталогов;
- корректно выбирает версию: точное совпадение, максимальная в линейке или максимальная найденная;
- выдаёт диагностику с перечислением проверенных каталогов и доступных версий при ошибке.

## Что изменено

- **`packagedef`** — добавлена зависимость `edtfind`.
- **`src/Классы/ВыгрузкаКонфигурацииВГит.os`**:
  - добавлена функция `ОпределитьПутьК1cedtcli()`, которая при явно заданном `ПутьКЕДТ` проверяет наличие `1cedtcli` в указанном каталоге, а иначе делегирует поиск библиотеке `edtfind`;
  - в процедуре конвертации в формат ЕДТ условие выбора новой версии CLI упрощено: вместо проверки `ПутьКЕДТ` и сравнения версий теперь используется результат `ОпределитьПутьК1cedtcli()`;
  - параметр `ПутьК1cedtcli` передаётся в `КонвертироватьВФорматЕДТ_НоваяВерсияCLI` явно, вместо повторного поиска внутри процедуры;
  - удалены функции `НайтиКаталогУстановкиЕДТ()` и `КаталогиУстановкиЕДТПоУмолчанию()`, логика которых теперь покрывается `edtfind`.

## Обратная совместимость

Внешний API yard (параметры командной строки) не изменён. При явно заданном пути к EDT поведение сохраняется. При автоматическом поиске EDT алгоритм `edtfind` покрывает те же каталоги по умолчанию (Windows и Linux), что и удалённый код.

author: danfurbs
body:
### Motivation
- Future (purple) MST instances were only receiving a minimal set of fields which caused their displayed details to drift from the base (green) MST, especially for MSTs loaded from Excel or when creating/amending MSTs.
- The change aims to ensure UI consumers that read event `extendedProps` see consistent information across base and future instances.

### Description
- Snapshot the base event `extendedProps` into a `baseExtendedProps` object and pass it into `E.storeVirtualInstances` so virtual instances carry a copy of the full base payload.
- Include `baseExtendedProps` on each virtual instance and merge `...(inst.baseExtendedProps || {})` into the `extendedProps` when creating rendered future events so instance-specific fields still override correctly.
- Update `E.rebuildFutureInstances` to capture `baseEvent.extendedProps` and forward it into the virtual store so rebuilds (for Excel-loaded, newly created, or amended MSTs) preserve base details.

### Testing
- Ran `node --check docs/libs/mst-editor-logic.js` which completed successfully.

body:
Sometimes, after thermal-update service stop we can get error message
hw-management-thermal-updater.service: Failed with result "'timeout'
It happens because we have in code long Event.wait().
It kept the main thread in a C-level wait, so the SIGTERM handler never
ran and systemd killed the service after TimeoutStopSec.

Fix: add Wait in small chunks via _exit_wait() so the handler runs and
the process
exits cleanly. Applied to in thermal-updater and peripheral-updater
