author: gmanojds
body:
## Fix: Handle null EclipseStore root during SQLite migration

### Problem
During startup, Reaper initializes SQLite and then attempts to migrate legacy EclipseStore data if `channel_*` artifacts are present.

In some upgrade scenarios, EclipseStore files exist but the root object is `null`. This causes migration to fail with:
```Unexpected root type: null```
As a result, Reaper fails to start even though there is no actual data to migrate.

### Root Cause
Migration is triggered purely based on the presence of `channel_*` files.

However:
- EclipseStore storage may exist without a persisted root object
- In such cases, `eclipseStore.root()` returns `null`
- Current code treats this as a fatal condition instead of an empty state

---

### Fix
- Treat `root == null` as an empty legacy state (non-fatal)
- Skip data migration and allow startup to continue
- Ensure EclipseStore artifacts are still backed up

author: wenjieshen
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a shared image texture cache for the GL renderer.

- add `GlImageTextureCache` to retain textures by `RenderSurface` + filter mode
- reuse existing GL textures instead of re-uploading the same image for every draw
- track image texture ownership in `GlShape`
- release cached textures when the last user goes away
- clear cached textures on renderer teardown and when the GL context changes

## Why

The previous path uploaded a fresh texture per image render object, even when multiple draws referenced the same source image. This change separates texture lifetime management from draw submission and gives the renderer a reusable primitive for later batching work.

## Performance

I have performed a targeted comparison of an image benchmark (5k duplicated image) between the jay/exp/image-shared-texture branch and the main branch, using 5 runs for increased stability.
The experimental branch shows a significant performance improvement of approximately 3.3x for image rendering.

| Scene | Ratio |
| -- | -- |
| default | 3.35x |
| rotated | 3.32x |

All examples don't have regression.

Configures the repo for Firebase — Firestore database, Email/Password authentication, Firebase Hosting, and C# Admin SDK setup — with no build tooling required on the frontend.

## New Files

- **`.env.example`** — credential template for all `FIREBASE_*` env vars
- **`.gitignore`** — adds `.env`, `serviceAccountKey.json`, Firebase debug logs, `.firebase/`
- **`firebase.json`** — hosting (`frontend/`), Firestore rules/indexes, emulator ports (Auth: 9099, Firestore: 8080, Hosting: 5001, UI: 4000)
- **`.firebaserc`** — project alias placeholder
- **`firestore.rules`** — security rules mirroring the existing role model: `Munshid` read-only, `LeadMunshid` full CRUD across all collections
- **`firestore.indexes.json`** — composite index placeholder
- **`frontend/js/firebase-config.js`** — Firebase JS SDK v10 via CDN (no build step); exports `app`, `db`, `auth` and helpers: `getPoems`, `getPoemById`, `addPoem`/`updatePoem`/`deletePoem`, `subscribeToCurrentState`, `shareCurrentState`, `signIn`, `signOutUser`, `onAuthChange`
- **`package.json`** — declares `firebase ^10.12.2`, `firebase-tools` devDep, and deploy/emulator npm scripts
- **`FIREBASE_SETUP.md`** — end-to-end guide: project creation, credential injection, Firestore data model, C# Admin SDK wiring, hosting deploy, emulator usage

## Design Notes

- Credentials injected at runtime via `window.__FIREBASE_*__` globals — no secrets hard-coded
- All Firestore writes use `serverTimestamp()` to avoid client clock skew
- CDN SDK import matches the project's existing no-build-tools frontend convention

## Usage Example

```js
// Subscribe to live current poem/wasla (real-time)
import { subscribeToCurrentState } from './firebase-config.js';

const unsub = subscribeToCurrentState(state => {
  if (state?.type === 'poem') {
    document.getElementById('current-poem-title').textContent = state.payload.title;
  }
});
```

body:
Tag all SnQL API errors with referrer, tenant_ids, and source:snql_api to improve error tracking and debugging in production.

## What

Adds a new `_set_snql_api_error_tags()` helper function that sets Sentry tags early in the SnQL API request lifecycle. This ensures any error (during parsing, validation, or query execution) includes:

- `source: snql_api` - identifies the API source
- `referrer` - from HTTP header or request body
- `tenant_ids` - as Sentry context for structured data
- Individual `tenant_id.*` tags (e.g., `tenant_id.organization_id`) for easier filtering

## Why

Currently when errors occur in the SnQL API, they lack contextual information about which tenant/organization triggered them. This makes it difficult to:
- Filter errors by organization or project in Sentry
- Identify patterns in errors from specific referrers
- Debug production issues quickly

With these tags, we can immediately see which organization, project, and referrer are associated with each error, enabling faster triaging and debugging.

author: mahendrarathore1742
body:
This PR fixes a critical bug where the standard [print()](vscode-file://vscode-app/home/msr/Desktop/VSCode-linux-x64/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) function in Mojo would crash with an illegal instruction (SIGILL) on CPUs that do not support AVX, due to unconditional use of AVX instructions (e.g., vmovups) in numeric-to-string conversions.

### **Adds** runtime detection for AVX support in the SIMD library.
- Falls back to SSE4.2 or scalar code paths if AVX is not available.
- Ensures numeric types (e.g., Int32) can be safely printed on older or entry-level hardware, matching the documented minimum requirement of SSE4.2 for Mojo.
- No unnecessary code or comments; clean and minimal patch.

Fixes #6257

author: copilot
body:
`python build.py` crashes immediately on Windows when the terminal uses cp1252 (or similar) encoding because the `print` statements contain emoji and Vietnamese characters that cp1252 cannot encode.

## Changes

- **`build.py`**: Reconfigure `sys.stdout` to UTF-8 at module level before any `print` calls, with `errors="replace"` as a safe fallback. Guarded by `hasattr` for environments where stdout has been replaced with a non-`TextIOWrapper`.

```python
if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
```

author: acpaquette
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

## Description
Issues arise when comparing cameras to map projected images in qview, and likely other ISIS QApps. As noted in issues in the related issues sections. Projected images where scaling differently when compared to the associated images with just a camera model. This is due to the `distancePerPixel` method in the FindTool.

There are two situations to consider with this problem:

1. Comparing an image with camera information to a projected image with the same camera information
2. Comparing a projected image with no camera information to a the same projected image with camera information

The FindTool requests the radii from either the camera or the projection depending on what is present. The old behavior always used the camera which is fine for situation 1.

There are instances in ISIS where one can create an identical projected product but remove the old camera information (automos, and other mosaic apps where only one image is used). In these cases comparing a camera to the projection in the old code resulted in scale disparities, see the UniversalGroundMap class and the FindTool classes `distancePerPixel` function. This issue arose in situation 2.

If we fix situation 2 by forcing to use the projection as the priority we introduce the same bug/issues into situation 1. 

This PR allows users to select the projection priority so that both situations can be accessed by users.

## Related Issue
#5896
#5508

### Motivation

- Provide a local, desktop-first web interface for frame-first color grading of videos with realtime browser preview and presets.
- Allow users to export the current filtered frame as PNG and render full MP4 exports (single or batch per preset) using `ffmpeg` on the backend.
- Keep slider interactions responsive by performing live pixel math in the browser and approximate the same look for exports via FFmpeg filter graphs.

### Description

- Add a Flask backend (`video_color_editor/app.py`) that implements upload (`/upload`), single export (`/export`), batch export (`/batch_export`), and static serving for `uploads` and `outputs`, plus helper functions to build FFmpeg filter chains and run `ffmpeg` (`run_ffmpeg`, `build_base_chain`, `hex_to_rgb_triplet`).
- Add frontend assets under `video_color_editor/static/` including `app.js` which implements slider UI, presets, canvas-based realtime frame processing, export handlers, and batch UI, and `styles.css` for the UI.

- Implement a set of predefined presets (`PRESETS`) and normalization/clamping of incoming settings (`normalize_settings`) to protect the FFmpeg invocation and ensure safe user input.

## Problem

The Express wrapper was defaulting to port 8080 (PORT) and the internal gateway was defaulting to port 9000 (INTERNAL_GATEWAY_PORT), which conflicted with the expected configuration where the gateway should listen locally on 8080.

## Solution

Changed PORT default from 8080 to 3000 (public-facing Express wrapper) and INTERNAL_GATEWAY_PORT default from 9000 to 8080 (internal loopback gateway). The gateway now binds to 127.0.0.1:8080 and Express proxies to it from port 3000, matching the configuration the user was instructed to use.

body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: Most parties only had explicit relationships with 2-3 others. Missing pairs defaulted to `1.0` (full acceptance) via `relationshipValue()`, allowing impossible coalitions like V+SF supported by EL to score ~5% probability.
- **Fix**: Added explicit `inGov`, `asSupport`, `tolerateInGov`, and `asPM` values for all 12×11 directed party pairs across EL, ALT, DF, DD, BP, LA, KF, RV, SF, S, and V. Cross-bloc pairs (e.g. EL→V, SF→DF, ALT→LA) are set near zero. Within-bloc pairs (e.g. V→KF, EL→SF) reflect realistic alliance potential.
- **Impact**: Eliminates implausible coalitions (V+SF on EL mandates) and should produce more realistic relative probabilities between plausible coalitions.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run simulator with default parameters and verify V+SF no longer appears in top coalitions
- [ ] Verify S+RV+SF and S+M+SF+RV still appear with reasonable relative probabilities
- [ ] Check that blue-bloc coalitions (V+LA+KF etc.) still form when blue has majority
- [ ] Spot-check that no new implausible cross-bloc coalitions have appeared

author: copilot
body:
`DecimalType(p, s)` where `p <= s` (e.g., `DecimalType(1,1)`, `DecimalType(2,2)`) causes Hive ORC to corrupt zero values like `0.0`, `0.00`. Additionally, `Literal(JavaBigDecimal)` was using raw BigDecimal precision instead of Spark's adjusted `Decimal` precision, leading to invalid `DecimalType` construction for values where `precision < scale`.

## Changes

- **`OrcFileFormat.scala`** — `sanitizeDecimalType` now rewrites any `DecimalType(p, s)` where `p <= s` to ensure at least one integer digit. Handles the `scale >= MAX_PRECISION` boundary explicitly by capping to `DecimalType(MAX_PRECISION, MAX_PRECISION - 1)` rather than attempting to set `precision = scale + 1 > 38`.

- **`literals.scala`** — `Literal(JavaBigDecimal)` now derives `DecimalType` from `Decimal`'s adjusted precision/scale (which correctly handles cases like `0.00` where raw `BigDecimal.precision < BigDecimal.scale`), then bounds both values to `MAX_PRECISION` to prevent `AnalysisException` for large-scale inputs (e.g., `0.` with 38 fractional digits).

  ```scala
  // Before: raw BigDecimal precision could be < scale → invalid DecimalType
  Literal(decimal, DecimalType(d.precision(), d.scale()))
  
  // After: use Spark-adjusted precision, bounded to MAX_PRECISION
  val decimal = Decimal(d)
  val boundedPrecision = math.min(DecimalType.MAX_PRECISION, decimal.precision)
  val boundedScale = math.min(boundedPrecision, decimal.scale)
  Literal(decimal, DecimalType(boundedPrecision, boundedScale))
  ```

- **`HiveOrcSourceSuite.scala`** — Regression test covering write/read round-trip for `DecimalType(1,1)`, `(2,2)`, `(3,3)`. Verifies zero values aren't corrupted, and that reading with the original schema preserves both type and scale for zero and non-zero values.

- **`LiteralExpressionSuite.scala`** — Tests that `Literal(JavaBigDecimal)` infers `precision > scale` for zero values (`0.0`, `0.00`, etc.) including the MAX_PRECISION boundary case (`0.` with 38 fractional digits).

body:
Claude's explanation of the issue:

**Problem**: `SkyDocsHeadingAnchorService.#getLinks()` used `document.querySelectorAll('sky-docs-heading-anchor')` to find and sort registered anchors by DOM position. When heading anchors were rendered inside structural directives like `@if`, Angular's `ngAfterViewInit` fired (triggering register) before the elements were attached to the document. Since `querySelectorAll` couldn't find those elements, they were silently dropped from the emitted links array, causing the table of contents to appear empty.

**Fix**: Instead of querying the DOM, the service now stores each anchor's native element reference in a `Map` during `register()`. The `#getLinks()` method sorts using `compareDocumentPosition` on those stored references, ensuring all registered anchors are always included regardless of their attachment timing. A secondary `splice` bug (missing the `deleteCount` argument, causing it to remove all anchors after the target) was also fixed.

Adds `providerAutoSelected` boolean to `RampsControllerState` and an `options` parameter to `setSelectedProvider` so callers can mark a provider as system-guessed (soft selection) vs user-chosen (hard selection).

## Summary

- Auto-select first suggestion when stdin is not a TTY (CI, subprocess capture, editor integrations like Claude Code)
- Harden `getch()` to catch `termios.error` instead of crashing in non-terminal contexts
- Matches existing `--yeah` behavior — no new flags or config needed

## Problem

When `thefuck` runs in a non-TTY context (e.g. piped through `$()` in a subprocess, CI pipelines, AI coding assistants), `termios.tcgetattr()` in `getch()` crashes with:

```
termios.error: (25, 'Inappropriate ioctl for device')
```

This happens because the interactive key-reading path is reached even when there's no terminal to read from.

## Changes

- **`thefuck/ui.py`**: Added `_is_interactive()` TTY check in `select_command()`. When no TTY is detected, auto-selects the first suggestion (same behavior as `--yeah`)
- **`thefuck/system/unix.py`**: Hardened `getch()` to catch `termios.error` and return `'\n'` (auto-select) as a defense-in-depth fallback

## Test plan

- [x] Verified `_is_interactive()` returns `False` in subprocess context
- [x] Verified `getch()` returns `'\n'` instead of crashing without TTY
- [x] Verified full `thefuck` flow works in non-TTY (auto-selects first suggestion)

author: exokomodo-bot
body:
## Problem

Direct navigation to sub-routes like `/photos` or `/health` (via browser address bar or page refresh) redirects to `/` and lands on the Cirrus page instead of the intended page. In-app navigation works fine.

## Root cause

`c.FileFromFS("public/index.html", http.FS(public))` in the NoRoute handler internally sets the request path and delegates to Go's `http.FileServer`, which has built-in behavior to redirect `/dir/index.html` requests to `/dir/` ([fs.go#L593](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/a7e16abb22f1b249d2691b32a5d20206282898f2/src/net/http/fs.go#L593)). This strips the original URL path before Flutter's router ever sees it.

## Fix

Read `index.html` once at startup from the embedded FS, then serve it via `c.Data(200, "text/html", indexHTML)` in the NoRoute handler. `c.Data` writes the response directly with no redirect, so the browser URL stays as `/photos` and Flutter's client-side router handles the path correctly.

## Testing

- Direct navigation to `/cirrus`, `/photos`, `/health`, `/settings` should all land on the correct page
- Page refresh on any route should reload the same page
- API routes (`/api/v1/*`) are unaffected (matched before NoRoute)
- Static assets (JS, CSS, images) are unaffected (served by `static.Serve` middleware)

Closes #842

author: pranavharlalka
body:
This pull request updates the `BookMyStay.java` application to focus on robust error handling and input validation for booking requests. It replaces the previous booking history and reporting logic with a new workflow that validates user input before processing bookings, introduces domain-specific error handling, and centralizes validation and inventory management. The changes also add a queue-based system for managing booking requests in a fair, first-in-first-out manner.

**Major changes include:**

**Input Validation and Error Handling:**
- Replaces the booking history/reporting flow with a new workflow that prompts for user input, validates the guest name and room type, and handles errors using a custom `InvalidBookingException`. User input is only accepted if it passes all validation checks.

- Adds the `InvalidBookingException` class for clear, domain-specific error handling when bookings are invalid.

- Introduces the `ReservationValidator` class to centralize all booking validation rules, ensuring consistent and maintainable validation logic.

**Room Inventory Management:**
- Adds the `RoomInventory` class as the single source of truth for room availability, supporting initialization, querying, and updating of room counts for each room type.

**Booking Request Management:**
- Introduces the `BookingRequestQueue` class, which manages booking requests using a FIFO queue to ensure fair processing of requests.

**Other:**
- Updates imports to include only necessary classes for the new workflow and removes unused ones.

These changes collectively improve the robustness, maintainability, and fairness of the booking process by validating input, handling errors gracefully, and centralizing key logic.

body:
### Ticket
[#40745 
](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/40745)

### Problem description
Device ops without an overridden `compute_program_hash` (e.g. layernorm) uses the default `device_operation` implementation. This hashes the input tensor objects, which attempts to hash the underlying storage() object. This crashes for default-constructed Tensors where storage has not been allocated yet.

### What's changed
Implement a Tensor::to_hash() function that hashes nullptr attributes in a stable way

This PR also exposed compute_program_hash for layernorm to Python for testing the repro case in #40745.

## Summary

- Remove the buggy `LazyFileBuffer` class and all references
- Implement two-stage buffer model: Source Buffer uses Heap memory, Filtered Buffer uses Network Buffer Pool, eliminating deadlock during channel state recovery
- Add `SpillingBufferManager` with three-path routing (P1 Memory / P2 Spill / P3 Replay) for filtered buffers when Network Buffer Pool is exhausted
- Add `SpillFileWriter`/`SpillFileReader` for length-prefixed spill file I/O with channel context
- Add checkpoint integration via `createCheckpointIterator()` with reference counting to prevent premature file deletion

author: copilot
body:
`TypeResolver.Resolve()` called `GetService(type)` which returns `null` on construction failure. Spectre.Console.Cli converts `null` into its own generic `"Could not resolve type 'XXX'"` error, swallowing the real cause (e.g., unconfigured `keyVault:vaultUri`, bad URI, Azure CLI credential failure).

## Description

- **`TypeRegistrar.cs`** — swap `GetService` → `GetRequiredService` in `TypeResolver.Resolve()` so actual DI exceptions propagate instead of being silently converted to `null`

```csharp
// Before — swallows construction failures
return serviceProvider.GetService(type);

// After — throws the real exception
return serviceProvider.GetRequiredService(type);
```

- **`TypeRegistrarTests.cs`** — update `Build_ReturnsTypeResolverThatReturnsNullForUnregisteredType` to expect `InvalidOperationException` (renamed to `Resolve_WhenTypeIsNotRegistered_ThrowsInvalidOperationException`); add `Resolve_WhenRegisteredTypeHasFailingDependency_ThrowsActualException` to pin the propagation behavior; explicitly dispose the `TypeResolver` via `((IDisposable)resolver).Dispose()` in all tests to prevent `ServiceProvider` leaks across test runs

author: punkercelestial
body:
O CMakeLists.txt apresenta uma violação de sintaxe no comando file(GLOB_RECURSE SPHEN_SRC PUBLIC ...). O PUBLIC é um token inválido nesse contexto, pois a assinatura correta do comando é file(GLOB_RECURSE <variable> [<globbing expressions>...]). Qualquer argumento extra, como PUBLIC, é interpretado como parte dos padrões de globbing, resultando em uma tentativa de expandir um padrão literal PUBLIC – o que não corresponde a nenhum arquivo e, mais grave, em versões recentes do CMake (≥3.0) causa um erro fatal na fase de configuração, abortando a geração do sistema de build. Esse erro é crítico porque impede completamente a compilação do projeto.

A origem provável do PUBLIC é uma confusão com a sintaxe de target_sources(), onde PUBLIC é um modificador válido para definir a visibilidade de fontes. No entanto, file(GLOB_RECURSE) é uma operação puramente de listagem de arquivos, sem relação com alvos ou escopos. A correção consiste em simplesmente remover o PUBLIC, resultando em:

cmake
file(GLOB_RECURSE SPHEN_SRC
        "str.c"
        "debug.c"
        "tokens.c"
        "lexer.c"
        "ast.c"
        "parser.c"
)
Após essa alteração, a variável SPHEN_SRC é corretamente preenchida com os caminhos dos arquivos encontrados, e o executável Sphen é construído sem interrupções. Nenhuma outra linha do arquivo é modificada; flags como -fsanitize=address e CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Debug permanecem intactas. Trata-se de uma correção localizada, de baixo risco, que restaura a funcionalidade básica do sistema de build.

author: rorybyrne
body:
## Summary

- **Ingest domain (#104)**: Batch-native ingestion pipeline for bulk scientific databases (PDB, GEO, UniProt). Records flow Ingester → Hooks → Record, bypassing the deposition lifecycle. Batches 100 records per hook invocation for throughput (PDB: 200k+ structures).
- **OOM retry with memory doubling (#105)**: When a hook container OOMs, automatically retry with 2x memory (1g → 2g → 4g → 8g, max 3 retries). Checkpoints partial progress between retries so completed records aren't reprocessed. Works for both batch ingestion and single-record deposition validation.
- **File-size sorting**: Records sorted smallest-first before hook execution to maximize checkpoint progress before a potential OOM on a large record.
- **SDK file size tracking**: `IngesterFileRef.size_mb` (required) computed automatically during download. `max_file_mb` on `@ingester` decorator silently skips oversized records at the entrypoint.
- **Type safety**: `OutcomeStatus` enum replaces stringly-typed status fields; `HookRecordId` NewType for record IDs in batch outcomes.

## Key changes

- New `ingest/` domain with `IngestRun` aggregate, `RunIngester`/`RunHooks`/`PublishBatch` event handlers
- New `HookService` in `validation/service/hook.py` — shared by both deposition and ingestion pathways
- `HookStatus.OOM` enum value distinguishes OOM from generic failure in both OCI and K8s runners
- `HookDefinition.with_doubled_memory()` for memory escalation
- `HookStoragePort` extended with `write_checkpoint()` and `write_batch_outcomes()`
- `ValidationService.run_hooks()` delegates to `HookService` for per-hook OOM retry
- `StorageLayout` consolidates all path resolution for ingests, hooks, and depositions
- Migration: `ingest_runs` table for tracking bulk ingestion state

## Test plan

- [x] 970 server unit tests passing (including 12 new HookService tests, 2 new ValidationService OOM tests, 6 IngesterRecord tests)
- [x] 223 SDK tests passing (including 4 new ingester entrypoint max_file_mb tests, 3 new IngesterFileRef tests)
- [x] Lint clean (`ruff check`)
- [ ] End-to-end: run RCSB PDB ingestion with `max_file_mb=40`, verify oversized records skipped, hooks process remaining records, OOM retry triggers on memory-intensive structures

Closes #104, closes #105

author: kenbolton
body:
Follow-up fixes to #1448 (`channel-formatting` skill).

## Changes

### 1. Preserve Telegram links — `skill/channel-formatting` branch

`[text](url)` links were being flattened to `text (url)` for all non-Slack channels. Telegram Markdown v1 renders inline links natively, so they should be passed through unchanged. Only WhatsApp (which doesn't support Markdown links) gets the flattened form.

Updates the `SKILL.md` table to reflect correct Telegram behaviour.

### 2. Tighten `splitProtectedRegions` regex — `skill/channel-formatting` branch

Old pattern: `` /```[\s\S]*?```/g `` — matched ` ``` ` anywhere in a line, causing false-positive code-block protection when backtick-triples appeared mid-line.

New pattern: `` /^```[^\n]*\n[\s\S]*?\n```$/gm `` — requires the fence to start and end at a line boundary and allows a language specifier.

### 3. Preserve trailing newline after code blocks in `parseSignalStyles` — `skill/channel-formatting` branch

The `\n` after a closing ` ``` ` was previously swallowed, running the next paragraph directly into the code block content in the output string.

## Tested

- `npx vitest run src/formatting.test.ts` — 75/75 passing
- New test case: Telegram link preservation

body:
Been cooking on this for some time now, and testing during horde survival sessions, I think it's ready for a PR. Please let me know if you have any questions, concerns, feedback, etc - Ill give a general rundown here

Overview:
- The freecam is a clientside-only player_t with id 255 that is added during G_InitNew, if we are in a netdemo or survival gamemode
- The freecam is in the rotation for spynext/spyprev
- The consoleplayer's commands are copied to the displayplayer if the displayplayer is the freecam (allow control)
- The freecam position is saved for rewind/fastforward in demos, and will reset on level/wad change
- The freecam is usable in survival only when you run out of lives
- The majority of code paths are handled by the freecam being a spectator as well as ingame() equating to false. Anything else that was needed (like allow mouse movement) checks the new bool isFreecam (default false)

Confirmed during testing:
- Odasrv is never told about the freecam player and never sees it
- The freecam player is never serialized (meaning when you are in survival game and recording a netdemo - the freecam player is not written to that netdemo)
- The clientside freecam will retire and become unusable if a real 255th player joins the game/netdemo (tested this by setting freecamplayer_id to 2 instead of 255)

Note I started another implementation where freecam was it's own real object (not static), and both Freecam and player_t inherited from a base class. However that was quickly scrapped because I realized the codebase is chained to player_t and any attempt to untangle would require a herculean rewrite. - that being said I think this works quite well!

author: niklas9234
body:
### Motivation
- Replace fragile string-based reasoning for forced replans with an explicit control flag to make policy -> engine interactions clearer and more type-safe. 
- Decouple metrics from opaque engine `reason` strings so trigger information is derived from policy/actor type instead of passed-through strings. 
- Make policy decision flow explicit (`decision = policy.decide(...)`) to simplify call sites and remove the old `(should_replan, reason)` tuple API.

### Description
- Replace `PolicyDecision.reason` with `PolicyDecision.allow_when_not_dirty: bool = False` and update all policy implementations (`PeriodicReplanPolicy`, `EventBasedReplanPolicy`, `StaticOnceReplanPolicy`, `PathAffectedReplanPolicy`, `NoReplanPolicy`) to return the new decision shape.  (`core/src/core/simulation/replan_policy.py`) 
- Change `SimulationEngine.replan(...)` signature to accept `allow_when_not_dirty` and `trigger_kind` instead of a string `reason`, and update the dirty-guard to `if not dirty_replan and not allow_when_not_dirty: return False`.  (`core/src/core/simulation/engine.py`) 
- Migrate callers in the simulation loop and experiment execution to use `decision = policy.decide(PolicyContext.from_state(...))` and pass `decision.allow_when_not_dirty` and a derived `trigger_kind` (policy type name) into `engine.replan(...)`.  (`core/src/core/simulation/loop.py`, `core/src/core/experiments/execution.py`) 
- Decouple metrics by replacing the `reason` parameter with `trigger_kind` in `MetricsRecorder.on_replan(...)` and keep the final run report key `replan_trigger_reason` populated from the `trigger_kind`/policy type for backward-compatible reports.  (`core/src/core/metrics/recorder.py`) 
- Update tests to assert the new decision flag/behavior and add a regression test ensuring forced replanning works when `dirty_replan` is false via the explicit flag.  (tests under `core/tests/`)

### Testing
- Ran targeted test suites with `pytest core/tests/test_experiment_policies.py core/tests/test_loop.py core/tests/test_metrics.py core/tests/test_engine.py` and confirmed the updated behavior. 
- All tests in the run completed successfully: `41 passed`. 
- The test set includes a regression test that verifies `replan(..., allow_when_not_dirty=True)` can force a replan when `dirty_replan` is false.

author: olvikt
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce split-brain/stale courier runtime state observed at polling/reconnect boundaries where UI-local toggles can outlive canonical backend state and where tracker watch may not start after reload/login. 
- Target the highest-risk flows without redesigning realtime architecture: UI polling drift for `online` and tracker reconnect/self-heal for geolocation watch. 
- Preserve fast UX for toggle events but add bounded optimism and explicit repair paths so inconsistencies self-heal.

### Description
- Introduced a short optimistic TTL in `AvailableOrders` so a `courier-online-toggled` UI event is honored briefly, then the component forces re-sync from canonical backend on subsequent render/poll by adding `UI_OPTIMISTIC_SYNC_TTL_SECONDS`, `lastUiOnlineSyncAt` and `repairOnlineStateFromCanonicalSource()` in `app/Livewire/Courier/AvailableOrders.php`.
- Added explicit runtime resync emission in `LocationTracker::mount()` so backend-driven repair is signalled to frontend with canonical runtime snapshot by dispatching `courier:runtime-sync` from `app/Livewire/Courier/LocationTracker.php`.
- Made frontend map runtime idempotently react to the resync event by listening for `courier:runtime-sync` and starting/stopping the geolocation watch accordingly in `resources/js/poof/map.js`, providing an explicit reconnect/self-heal path for the watch lifecycle.
- Added/strengthened tests: a new regression test asserting that optimistic UI state is self-healed after the grace window in `tests/Feature/Courier/AvailableOrdersOnlineSyncTest.php`, and strengthened the `LocationTracker` mount test to assert the `courier:runtime-sync` event payload in `tests/Feature/Courier/CourierRuntimeStateSyncTest.php`.

### Testing
- Syntax checks passed: `php -l` for modified PHP files succeeded and `node --check resources/js/poof/map.js` succeeded. 
- Ran unit/feature test runner but environment lacks autoload (`vendor/autoload.php`), so full `php artisan test` could not be executed in this sandbox (error: missing vendor). 
- Livewire assertions added in tests validate event dispatches and polling self-heal logic; new/updated tests were committed and are expected to pass in CI where `composer install` is available.

body:
## Summary

Research-driven context optimization based on `docs/research/mcp-optimization-research.md`.

### T1: Session-level guard dedup (94% reduction on repeated fires)
- Hash-based dedup tracks injected context per session
- Second+ injection returns one-liner reference instead of full context
- Applied to hazard and scope-drift guards

### T3: Top-3 hazard cap with recency ranking (65% first-fire reduction)
- Hazards sorted by most recent sprint, capped at top 3
- Shows overflow count with drill-down command
- 1502 chars → 530 chars on first fire

### T2: Compact briefing tier (98.7% reduction)
- `slope briefing --compact` produces L0 briefing: 343 chars vs 25,702
- Handicap, fairway/GIR, top hazards, claims, next sprint — in 5 lines

### T4: MCP search compact mode (~80% reduction on discovery)
- `search({})` returns name+description lines instead of full JSON
- `search({ compact: false })` for full detail

### Measured impact (this session: 986 turns)
- 131 Edit/Write fires × hazard guard: ~49k tokens → ~4k tokens (dedup + cap)

## Moving Wall Obstacle

Adds a new dynamic obstacle type - a narrow wall that moves from side to side across the track using sine wave oscillation.

### Changes
- **renderer.js**: Added moving wall generation, placement, animation, and visual rendering (purple/magenta with emissive glow)
- **main.js**: Integrated `updateMovingWalls()` into the game loop

### Key Design Decisions
- Walls spawn starting at distance 40 (level 3+) for progressive difficulty
- Width of 1.2 (narrower than static obstacles at 1.5) allows passing on either side
- Sine wave oscillation with randomized speed (1.2-2.0 rad/s) and phase offset

author: cdrage
body:
fix: prevent monitoring loop from spamming console when macadam is not installed

### What does this PR do?    
    
Moving the `macadamEvents.emit` call inside the try block so the monitoring    
loop only starts when `macadam.init()` succeeds.    
    
Previously, the event was emitted even when init failed, causing the 5-second monitoring loop     
torepeatedly try spawning `/usr/local/bin/macadam` and flooding the console    
with ENOENT errors.    
    
This is a Linux-only issue. On macOS, `areBinariesAvailable()` from    
`@crc-org/macadam.js` correctly checks if the binary exists on disk and    
returns `false` when missing, so `init()` is never called. On Windows,    
the macadam code path is skipped entirely. On Linux, `areBinariesAvailable()`    
unconditionally returns `true`, so `init()` is called even when macadam    
is not installed.    
    
I also opened up an issue upstream: https://github.com/crc-org/macadam.js/issues/146    
    
### What issues does this PR fix or reference?    
    
Resolves #2331                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
    
### How to test this PR?    
    
**Note:** This is a Linux-only issue and cannot be reproduced on macOS or Windows.    
    
1. On a Linux machine, ensure macadam is not installed (`whereis macadam`    
   should return nothing)    
2. Activate the bootc extension    
3. Confirm no repeated ENOENT errors in the console :)    

Signed-off-by: Charlie Drage <charlie@charliedrage.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

body:
### Motivation
- Users reported the candlestick chart not updating automatically and only refreshing after clicking the manual "Odśwież" button. 
- Investigation showed mixed refresh logic (full `setData(...)` reloads + a separate live-price updater) and possible HTTP caching causing stale responses. 
- The goal was to provide stable 1s realtime updates, avoid duplicated timers, and ensure indicators (EMA/RSI) update together with candles.

### Description
- Replaced the ad-hoc live-price / global-refresh mix with a dedicated 1s chart polling loop that queries `/api/candles` and applies incremental updates via `series.update(...)` for candles and indicator series.  
- Kept `setData(...)` only for the initial full load (`renderChartPayload`) and use `applyRealtimeChartUpdate` + `updateLineRealtime` to append/update only new points without recreating chart instances.  
- Added timer management (`startChartPolling`, `stopChartPolling`) and an in-flight guard (`chartPollingInFlight`) to prevent overlapping requests and duplicated intervals when switching pair or timeframe.  
- Added `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache` and `Pragma: no-cache` headers to `/api/candles` and `/api/price` responses to avoid stale data from browser/proxy caches; changed files: `static/app.js`, `app.py`.

### Testing
- Compiled Python modules with `python -m py_compile app.py screener.py storage.py order_bridge.py config_manager.py` and compilation succeeded.  
- Verified code changes by loading the page and observing console logs (polling lifecycle and realtime diagnostics) while polling `/api/candles` every second during development; no automated UI test harness was available in this environment.

author: gumclaw
body:
## What

Both the **PayoutInfo** and **MerchantAccounts** sections on the admin user page use `useIsIntersecting` to lazy-load data when they scroll into view. Before the fetch triggers or completes, they show misleading messages:

- "No payout info found." (PayoutInfo)
- "No merchant accounts." (MerchantAccounts)

This is confusing because the user may actually have payout/merchant data — it just hasn't loaded yet.

## Why

The components start with `isLoading: false` and `data: null`. Since the intersection observer hasn't fired yet, the render path hits the "no data" fallback immediately. There's no way to distinguish between "data hasn't been fetched yet" and "data was fetched and is genuinely empty."

## How

Added a `hasFetched` state flag to both components. A loading spinner shows until the fetch completes. The "no data" messages only appear after the API confirms there's nothing to show.

## Before / After

**Before** (current behavior — shows misleading "No payout info found" and "No merchant accounts" before async data loads):

The Payout Info section says "No payout info found" and Merchant Accounts says "No merchant accounts" even though this user (nushiai) has an ACH account at Wells Fargo and a Stripe merchant account. The data only appears after scrolling triggers the intersection observer.

**After** (with this fix):

A loading spinner shows in both sections until the async fetch completes. "No payout info" / "No merchant accounts" only displays after the API confirms there's genuinely no data.

## Testing

Verified on production (`/admin/users/nushiai`):
1. On initial page load (before scrolling to the section), the DOM shows "No payout info found" and "No merchant accounts"
2. After scrolling to trigger the intersection observer, the `/admin/users/{id}/payout_info` endpoint returns actual data (Wells Fargo ACH account, payouts paused by system)
3. The `/admin/users/{id}/merchant_accounts` endpoint also returns a Stripe merchant account
4. The fix ensures a loading spinner shows instead of the misleading empty-state messages until the fetch completes

author: copilot
body:
Adds `numerical_integration_methods.md` — a Russian-language reference note cataloguing ODE integrators applicable to rocket/trajectory dynamics, with orders of accuracy, method types, and selection guidance for delay/control problems.

## Coverage

- **Summary table** — 12 methods (Euler through symplectic Verlet): order *p*, explicit/implicit, single/multi-step, adaptive flag
- **Per-method sections** — key formulas and practical context for each integrator
- **Selection guide** — decision table mapping situation (paper estimate, stiff system, orbital arc, delay τ in control loop) to recommended method
- **Worked example** — ties methods to the marine launch platform problem (8 s swell, 2° tilt, 0.3 s delay, ±1 km accuracy requirement), showing how linearisation + RK4/ode45 + history buffer + Monte Carlo compose into a complete analysis

## Key guidance encoded

| Situation | Recommended method |
|---|---|
| Paper/Excel estimate | Heun (order 2) |
| Standard trajectory (non-stiff) | RK4 or ode45 (order 4/5, adaptive) |
| Stage separation / variable dynamics events | ode45 / Dormand–Prince |
| Stiff subsystems (TVC actuator, filters, structural modes) | BDF / ode15s (orders 1–6) |
| Long orbital arc, energy conservation | Verlet / Leapfrog (symplectic, order 2) |
| Delay τ in control loop | RK4 or ode45 + state history buffer; h ≪ τ |

author: nidhish-vartak
body:
This pull request introduces several backend and frontend improvements focused on security, user experience, and data integrity, especially around authentication, password reset, and location handling for society admins. Notably, it enforces stricter validation and error handling for password resets, improves audit logging for admin logins, and adds new columns to the `societies` table for precise location tracking. Additionally, it enhances frontend request activity tracking and email template design.

**Authentication & Password Reset Improvements:**

- Enforces stricter validation for password reset requests: now throws specific errors for missing, inactive, or non-existent emails, and exposes email delivery failures to the user instead of always returning success, improving both security and user feedback. 
- Updates the password reset email template for a more modern, user-friendly design.

**Society Admin Location & Audit Logging:**

- Requires society admins to be linked to a society and for that society to have an exact location set before login; login is blocked if these conditions are not met, and error messages are more precise.
- Changes login audit logic to always compare the admin's login location to the society's exact location, rather than previous login locations, for more accurate proximity checks. Also updates location audit on current login when the admin's location is updated. 

**Database Schema & Access Control:**

- Adds `exact_latitude` and `exact_longitude` columns to the `societies` table for precise location tracking, and updates schema migration logging.
- Adds or clarifies role-based access control annotations on endpoints for exporting tickets and managing society rules, and restricts certain attendance-related actions to committee and above (removes `MEMBER` role from these actions). 
**Frontend: Request Activity Tracking:**

- Implements a mechanism to track active API requests and connection failures in the frontend via a custom event, enabling the UI to react to network activity and errors more responsively.

author: emergentmonk
body:
Adds time-aware strategy analysis to QEC, enabling tracking of strategy behavior across runs, computation of trajectory metrics, and deterministic classification into behavioral regimes.

Key Additions
Strategy history tracking
Aggregates per-strategy metrics across runs
Deterministic ordering, no padding
Trajectory metrics
mean, variance, stability (1/(1+var))
trend (final − initial)
oscillation (sign changes of non-zero deltas only)
All values rounded to 12 decimals
Regime classification
stable, improving, declining, oscillatory, transitional
Deterministic rule-based system (no heuristics/ML)
Pipeline integration
runs → history → metrics → regimes
Added CLI flags:
--track-strategies
--show-trajectory
--show-regimes
Determinism Hardening
Zero-delta segments excluded from oscillation detection
Flat and single-point histories yield stable defaults
Fully reproducible, ambiguity-free trajectory semantics
Testing
33 tests covering:
determinism
metric correctness
regime classification
edge cases
no-mutation guarantees
Impact

Introduces time-awareness as a new analytical dimension:

evaluation → explanation → trajectory

QEC can now distinguish:

stable vs volatile strategies
improving vs declining behavior
oscillatory vs transitional dynamics

body:
### Summary

This pr closes #728 

This PR introduces a comprehensive notification system that keeps investors and operations teams informed about critical platform events. The implementation provides a flexible, scalable architecture for event-driven communications while remaining launch-ready with in-app delivery.

### What's Included

**Core Components:**

- **Database Schema** - New `notifications` table with support for 11 event types, 3 delivery channels, and delivery tracking with automatic retry logic
- **Repository Layer** - `NotificationRepository` with complete CRUD operations, advanced filtering (by user, event type, status), and pagination
- **Service Layer** - `NotificationService` with 20+ methods for creating notifications, triggering events, managing delivery state, and handling retries
- **API Layer** - `NotificationController` and routes exposing 7 RESTful endpoints for notification management
- **Comprehensive Tests** - 30+ test cases covering creation, retrieval, delivery state transitions, retry behavior, and idempotency


**Service Integrations:**

- KYC Controller: Automatic notifications on verification approval/rejection
- Lending Controller: Automatic notifications on loan repayments
- Risk Monitoring Controller: Automatic notifications on risk warnings and liquidation risks


**Event Categories:**

- Verification updates (approved/rejected)
- Repayment notifications (reminder/overdue/processed)
- Risk alerts (warning/liquidation)
- Valuation updates
- System alerts
- Investment opportunities


### Key Features

- Multi-channel delivery support (In-App, Email, SMS) with extensibility for future channels
- Automatic retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries
- Pagination and filtering capabilities for efficient notification retrieval
- Bulk operations (mark multiple as read, delete)
- Delivery status tracking and audit trail
- User-scoped access control
- Prevents duplicate notifications through idempotency checks
- Type-safe with full TypeScript coverage and Zod validation


### Launch Readiness

- In-app delivery fully implemented and tested
- Email and SMS channels ready for future implementation without redesign
- Professional, trustworthy message tones
- Production-ready error handling and validation


### Testing

All 30+ test cases pass, covering:

- Notification creation with various event types
- Filtering and pagination
- Delivery state management
- Retry logic behavior
- Bulk operations
- Idempotency and duplicate prevention


### Files Changed

- **New:** 7 files (~1,500 lines)

- `apps/api/src/db/schema/notifications.ts`
- `apps/api/src/repositories/NotificationRepository.ts`
- `apps/api/src/services/NotificationService.ts`
- `apps/api/src/controllers/NotificationController.ts`
- `apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts`
- `apps/api/src/__tests__/NotificationService.test.ts`

- `apps/api/src/app.ts` - Register notification routes

- `apps/api/src/controllers/KYCController.ts` - Integrate verification notifications
- `apps/api/src/controllers/LendingController.ts` - Integrate repayment notifications
- `apps/api/src/controllers/RiskMonitoringController.ts` - Integrate risk notifications



### Breaking Changes

None - this is a new feature with no impact on existing APIs

Yes - Run `002_create_notifications_table.sql` to create the notifications table and related indexes

Closes #27

Implements the `ChannelAdapter` interface and a working Slack adapter following the architecture described in `PHASE-5-ADAPTERS.md`.

## Changes

### `packages/gateway/src/adapters.ts` (new)
- Defines the `ChannelAdapter` interface: `name`, `init(sessionManager)`, `shutdown()`
- `initAdapters()` discovers adapters via env vars and initializes them at startup

### `packages/adapters/slack/src/index.ts` (was empty stub)
- `SlackAdapter` using `@slack/bolt` in Socket Mode
- Maps Slack threads (`channel + thread_ts`) to orchestrator sessions
- Streams agent responses back as threaded replies
- Ignores bot messages to prevent loops

### `packages/adapters/slack/package.json`
- Added `@slack/bolt` dependency
- Added `@openzosma/gateway` workspace dependency for type imports

### `packages/gateway/src/index.ts`
- Wires adapter initialization after server startup
- Graceful adapter shutdown on `SIGTERM`

## Configuration

Set these env vars to enable the Slack adapter:

```bash
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-...     # Required
SLACK_APP_TOKEN=xapp-...     # Required for Socket Mode
```

When `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is not set, the adapter is simply not loaded (zero impact on existing functionality).

## What's NOT in this PR (follow-ups)

- Valkey-based session mapping (currently uses in-memory Map -- sufficient for single-instance dev)
- Slack user -> OpenZosma user resolution via the `users` table
- HTTP Events API mode (for production multi-instance deployments)
- Message formatting (mrkdwn conversion, tool output as collapsed blocks)
- Rate limit handling and retry headers

Adds a reference doc covering the full `cloudflared` tunnel setup for the arcade-tracker Flask app running in the Proxmox LXC at `192.168.0.59`. Captures the live tunnel (`d98977c1-cc2c-43ac-8c86-86b7fd753ab1` → `tracker.greybardserver.com`) that is already operational.

- **Systemd service** — `cloudflared service install` + enable/start
- **Docker Compose alternative** — `cloudflared` sidecar with correct service-name networking note (`localhost:5000` → `arcade-tracker:5000`)
- **Troubleshooting** — error table for 1033 (tunnel not running), 1003 (DNS conflict), connection refused; plus quick-reference commands (`tunnel list`, `journalctl -u cloudflared -f`, etc.)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Create a new documentation file `CLOUDFLARED_SETUP.md` in the root of the repository that documents the complete process of setting up a Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`) for the arcade-tracker application running in a Proxmox LXC.

The document should cover the following, written as a reference guide:

## Context

- The arcade-tracker is a Flask app served on port 5000
- It runs inside a Proxmox LXC at `192.168.0.59`
- There is an existing ngrok tunnel (`arcade-tracker-ngrok.service`) that continues to work alongside this
- The Cloudflare Tunnel provides a stable, free, custom-domain alternative to ngrok
- The domain used is `tracker.greybardserver.com`
- The tunnel name is `tracker` and the tunnel UUID is `d98977c1-cc2c-43ac-8c86-86b7fd753ab1`

## Sections to include

### 1. Overview
- Brief explanation of what Cloudflare Tunnel does (connects origin server to Cloudflare's network without opening inbound ports)
- Why it was set up (stable custom domain, free, no port forwarding needed)
- Mention it runs alongside the existing ngrok tunnel

### 2. Prerequisites
- SSH access to the Proxmox LXC (`root@192.168.0.59` or `root@arcade-tracker`)
- A Cloudflare account with a domain added (e.g., `greybardserver.com`)
- The arcade-tracker Flask app running on port 5000

### 3. Installation
- Install `cloudflared` on the LXC:
  ```
  curl -L --output cloudflared.deb https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-linux-amd64.deb
  dpkg -i cloudflared.deb
  ```

### 4. Authentication
- Run `cloudflared tunnel login`
- Explains it generates a URL to open in a browser, select the domain, and authorize
- Saves `cert.pem` to `~/.cloudflared/`

### 5. Create the Tunnel
- Run `cloudflared tunnel create arcade-tracker` (or whatever name)
- Note the tunnel UUID that is output
- Credentials file saved to `~/.cloudflared/<TUNNEL_UUID>.json`

### 6. Configure the Tunnel
- Create `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml` with contents:
  ```yaml
  tunnel: d98977c1-cc2c-43ac-8c86-86b7fd753ab1
  credentials-file: /root/.cloudflared/d98977c1-cc2c-43ac-8c86-86b7fd753ab1.json

  ingress:
    - hostname: tracker.greybardserver.com
      service: http://localhost:5000
    - service: http_status:404
  ```

### 7. Route DNS
- If a conflicting DNS record exists, delete it first from the Cloudflare Dashboard
- Run: `cloudflared tunnel route dns tracker tracker.greybardserver.com`
- Explains this creates a CNAME record pointing to `<TUNNEL_UUID>.cfargotunnel.com`

### 8. Test the Tunnel
- Run: `cloudflared tunnel --config /etc/cloudflared/config.yml run tracker`
- Look for "Connection registered" in the output
- Test with `curl tracker.greybardserver.com` from another terminal
- Visit in browser to confirm

### 9. Install as a Persistent Service
- Run: `cloudflared service install`
- Then: `systemctl enable cloudflared` and `systemctl start cloudflared`
- Verify with: `systemctl status cloudflared`

### 10. Docker Compose Alternative (Optional)
- Show how to add a `cloudflared` sidecar service to `docker-compose.yml`:
  ```yaml
  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
    container_name: arcade-cloudflared
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: tunnel --config /etc/cloudflared/config.yml run
    volumes:
      - ./cloudflared:/etc/cloudflared
      - ./cloudflared:/root/.cloudflared
    networks:
      - arcade-net
    depends_on:
      - arcade-tracker
  ```
- Note: change `service: http://localhost:5000` to `service: http://arcade-tracker:5000` when using Docker networking

### 11. Troubleshooting
Include a table or section covering common errors:

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **1033** | Tunnel not running / doesn't exist | Start the tunnel daemon: `cloudflared tunnel run` |
| **1003** (DNS conflict) | An A/AAAA/CNAME record already exists for that hostname | Delete the conflicting record in the Cloudflare Dashboard first, then re-run `cloudflared tunnel route dns` |
| Connection refused | Flask app not running on port 5000 | Check `systemctl status arcade-tracker` or `docker ps` |

Also include useful commands:
- `cloudflared tunnel list` — list all tunnels
- `cloudflared tunnel info tracker` — show tunnel details
- `systemctl status cloudflared` — check service status
- `journalctl -u cloudflared -f` — follow tunnel logs
- `systemctl restart cloudflared` — restart the tunnel

### 12. Current Setup Reference
- Domain: `tracker.greybardserver.com`
- Tunnel name: `tracker`
- Tunnel UUID: `d98977c1-cc2c-43ac-8c86-86b7fd753ab1`
- Config file: `/etc/cloudflared/config.yml`
- Credentials: `/root/.cloudflared/d98977c1-cc2c-43ac-8c86-86b7fd753ab1.json`
- Service: `systemctl status cloudflared`
- App port: `5000`

## Summary

- **Layer 1:** Normalize RRF scores to 0-1 range in `_rrf_merge()` by dividing by theoretical max (1/k). Fixes all downstream filters that expected 0-1 scores but received ~0.033.
- **Layer 2:** Replace `_apply_relevance_floor()` + `_apply_diminishing_returns_cutoff()` with single `_apply_relevance_filter()` using adaptive min/max K bounds + gap detection.
- **Layer 3:** Remove legacy `TIER3_THRESHOLDS` blocks and `RELEVANCE_FLOORS`/`FLOOR_EXEMPT_SOURCES` from schemas.py.
- **Bonus fix:** Spreading activation was silently broken — seed scores at ~0.03 were below the 0.1 activation threshold. Normalization fixes this.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `nous/heart/search.py` | Add normalization to `_rrf_merge()` |
| `nous/cognitive/context.py` | Replace floor+cutoff with adaptive filter, remove TIER3 blocks |
| `nous/cognitive/schemas.py` | Remove `RELEVANCE_FLOORS`, `FLOOR_EXEMPT_SOURCES` |
| `nous/config.py` | Add `relevance_min_results`, `relevance_max_results` config |

3-agent architecture review (architect + search specialist + devil's advocate) completed. Key findings addressed:
- Score compression (0.845-1.0 with k=60) mitigated by downstream staleness/boost multipliers creating real spread

- `relevance_floor_enabled` config name kept for backward compatibility

author: andy963
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** Path traversal possible via partial directory match. The `startsWith` check on `resolved.startsWith(distClientDir)` allows matching sibling directories that share the same prefix (e.g., if `distClientDir` is `/app/dist`, an attacker requesting a path that resolves to `/app/dist-secrets` would bypass the check since `/app/dist-secrets`.startsWith(`/app/dist`) evaluates to true). Additionally, encoded paths could potentially bypass the `path.posix.normalize` logic.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could potentially access arbitrary files on the file system within sibling directories, or outside if encoded paths were manipulated correctly.
🔧 **Fix:** 
1. Added a `try/catch` block with `decodeURIComponent` to safely decode `req.url` before parsing.
2. Appended a path separator (`path.sep`) to the base directory before using `startsWith` to prevent partial matches, and allowed exact directory matches.
✅ **Verification:** Ran `pnpm test` and ensured all tests passed successfully. Verified locally that requests for `..%2f` and partial directory strings are rejected. Recorded findings in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: arthexis
body:
### Motivation

- Make upgrade gating logic pure and testable by separating decision-making from side-effectful execution. 
- Remove repeated `ensure_runtime_services(...)` calls spread across gating branches and centralize runtime/service handling. 
- Eliminate a duplicated recency check and compute recency once before decision construction to avoid inconsistent behavior and duplication.

### Description

- Added a typed decision model `AutoUpgradeDecision` and a pure `build_upgrade_decision(...)` function that returns `skip`, `apply`, `reason`, `args`, and `notify` describing the computed outcome. 
- Introduced `_execute_upgrade_decision(...)` as a thin executor that consumes the decision and centralizes logging, notifications (`notify`), `startup` hook invocation, and calls to `ensure_runtime_services(...)`, preserving previous log messages for each decision reason. 
- Removed the duplicated recency throttle check inside `_execute_upgrade_plan(...)` and compute recency once in `check_github_updates(...)`, passing it into `build_upgrade_decision(...)`. 
- Kept `_execute_upgrade_plan(...)` focused on running/delegating the upgrade and health checks; its behavior is preserved but simplified with the decision/executor split. 
- Exported `AutoUpgradeDecision` and `build_upgrade_decision` in module `__all__` and added mapping of decision reasons to existing log messages to preserve observability. 
- Added unit tests `apps/core/tests/test_auto_upgrade_decision.py` covering stable vs unstable, PyPI gating, canary gating, release revision mismatch gating, and recency throttling.

### Testing

- Prepared environment dependencies with `./env-refresh.sh --deps-only` and installed CI test deps from `requirements-ci.txt`. 
- Ran the new and related tests with `python manage.py test run -- apps/core/tests/test_auto_upgrade_decision.py apps/core/tests/test_auto_upgrade_canaries.py` and all tests passed (`8 passed`). 
- Ran style/import checks with `ruff` (`.venv/bin/ruff check --select I,UP035 apps/core/tasks/auto_upgrade/tasks.py apps/core/tests/test_auto_upgrade_decision.py`) and the import/format checks passed.

## Summary
- Remove the `terminalEnabled = !useTunnel` gate that disabled the integrated terminal when `--tunnel` was active
- The restriction provided no meaningful security benefit — an attacker with a valid auth token already has arbitrary code execution via agent sessions (`bypassPermissions`), making the terminal's capability delta effectively zero
- The real security boundary is the tunnel auth layer (token strength, TLS via Cloudflare, rotation)

author: rinchen
body:
## Summary

Adds `npm run linux` for Linux source development: wraps `sudo setpriv` (ambient `CAP_NET_RAW`) with display/auth and desktop session env preserved, then `npm start -- -no-sandbox`. Centralizes BLE capability messaging in `src/shared/linuxBleDevLaunch.ts`, updates in-app copy, terminal remediation, and documentation. Includes a follow-up fix to forward D-Bus and XDG-related env vars through `setpriv --reset-env` so BlueZ/session integration keeps working.

## What changed

- **Helper:** `scripts/linux-dev.mjs` and `package.json` script `linux`.
- **Shared copy:** `src/shared/linuxBleDevLaunch.ts` + `linuxBleDevLaunch.test.ts`; wired from `ConnectionPanel` and `noble-ble-manager`.
- **CLI hints:** `scripts/start-electron.mjs` remediation strings lead with `npm run linux`, then the manual setpriv one-liner.
- **Docs:** `docs/development-environment.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md` — primary path is `npm run linux` for Linux BLE + GUI from source.
- **Tests:** Contract, component, and start-electron test updates.

## Why

`@stoprocent/noble` on Linux needs raw sockets; ambient capability via setpriv avoids `setcap` on the dev Electron binary while keeping release guidance (setcap on packaged binary) separate. One module reduces drift between UI, main errors, and docs.

## How to test

- `npm run test:run`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`
- On Linux: from repo root, `npm run linux` (sudo for setpriv); confirm GUI starts and BLE scan path works.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Packaged Linux artifacts (`dist:linux`) unchanged; end users still use file capabilities on the installed binary per existing docs.

author: shivasurya
body:
## Summary

10 new Python security rules covering vulnerability patterns across archive extraction, template injection, cryptographic misuse, deserialization, CORS misconfiguration, and more.

## New Rules

| Rule ID | Pattern | Severity |
|---------|---------|----------|
| SEC-110 | Unsafe `tarfile.extractall()` / `extract()` without path validation | HIGH |
| SEC-113 | `HTTP_HOST` header used in access control decisions | MEDIUM |
| SEC-123 | Jinja2 SSTI via `from_string()` / `Template()` with untrusted input | HIGH |
| SEC-133 | RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 deprecated padding (Bleichenbacher risk) | HIGH |
| SEC-136 | Dynamic module import via `importlib.import_module()` / `load_object()` with user input | HIGH |
| SEC-138 | Cypher/graph query injection via string concatenation (CWE-943) | HIGH |
| SEC-139 | Unsafe `msgpack` deserialization with `ext_hook` object reconstruction | HIGH |
| SEC-144 | CORS wildcard `allow_origins=["*"]` with `allow_credentials=True` | HIGH |
| SEC-157 | `ZipFile.extract()` / `extractall()` path traversal (Zip Slip) | HIGH |
| SEC-162 | Symlink following leading to arbitrary file read (CWE-59) | HIGH |

## Real-World CVE Coverage

These rules detect patterns found in real-world advisories:

- **CVE-2007-4559** / [GHSA-fhff-qmm8-h2fp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhff-qmm8-h2fp) — tarfile path traversal (mlflow, 15+ years unfixed in stdlib)
- [GHSA-q485-cg9q-xq2r](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q485-cg9q-xq2r) — Host header authentication bypass (pyload)
- [GHSA-pxrr-hq57-q35p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxrr-hq57-q35p) — Jinja2 SSTI via config values (dynaconf)
- [GHSA-7432-952r-cw78](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7432-952r-cw78) — Bleichenbacher padding oracle (authlib)
- [GHSA-cwxj-rr6w-m6w7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cwxj-rr6w-m6w7) — Arbitrary module import via HTTP header (Scrapy)
- [GHSA-gg5m-55jj-8m5g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gg5m-55jj-8m5g) — Cypher injection in graph DB (graphiti-core)
- [GHSA-g48c-2wqr-h844](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g48c-2wqr-h844) — msgpack deserialization RCE (LangGraph)
- [GHSA-9jfm-9rc6-2hfq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9jfm-9rc6-2hfq) — CORS credential theft (Glances)
- [GHSA-8rrh-rw8j-w5fx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8rrh-rw8j-w5fx) — Zip Slip path traversal (wheel/setuptools)
- [GHSA-g925-f788-4jh7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g925-f788-4jh7) — Symlink arbitrary file read (Weblate)

## What's Included

Each rule has:
- `rule.py` — detection logic using the Python DSL (`QueryType`, `calls()`, `Or()`)
- `meta.yaml` — full metadata (CWE, OWASP mapping, description, secure examples, FAQ, compliance)
- `tests/positive/vulnerable.py` — vulnerable code patterns that trigger the rule
- `tests/negative/safe.py` — safe alternatives that should NOT trigger

## Test Results

All rules verified — positive tests detect, negative tests produce 0 false positives.

Root cause: DataTable.clear() + bulk add_row() drifts the viewport to the last added row. The cursor restore logic moved the logical cursor back but did not force the scroll viewport to follow.

Fix:
- Track user interaction via _user_moved_cursor flag (set on nav keys and toggle_selected)

- When user has interacted, restore their cursor position with animate=False
- Add safety clamp when table shrinks (old cursor index > new row count)

Includes regression test (test_process_tree_scroll.py) covering:
- Idle state pins to top
- User interaction preserves position
- Table shrink clamping

body:
### Motivation
- Construir a API backend necessária para a plataforma de gestão de dietas descrita no enunciado da UC, suportando nutricionistas, pacientes e administrador.
- Fornecer endpoints para autenticação, gestão de utilizadores, definição e acompanhamento de dietas e dashboards que permitam visualização de calorias e progresso.
- Publicar documentação básica OpenAPI/Swagger para facilitar exploração e integração do Client Angular obrigatório.

### Description
- Adiciona uma aplicação Express em `src/` com `src/app.js` e `src/server.js` e configuração de middlewares (`cors`, `morgan`, `express.json`) e rota de healthcheck `/health`.
- Implementa middleware de autenticação/autorizaçã o JWT em `src/middleware/auth.js` com helpers `authRequired`, `allowRoles` e `signToken` e expiração de 8h.
- Cria rotas modulares em `src/routes/` para `auth`, `admin`, `nutritionists`, `diets` e `dashboard` cobrindo registo/login, validação/CRUD de nutricionistas, criação de pacientes, criação/consulta de dietas (limite 5 refeições/dia) e registo de cumprimento de refeições com imagem obrigatória.
- Introduz armazenamento em memória e dados iniciais em `src/data/store.js`, documentação OpenAPI básica em `src/openapi.yaml`, `package.json` com dependências e atualização do `README.md` com instruções e credenciais iniciais.

### Testing
- Foi executado o verificador de sintaxe Node em todos os ficheiros principais com `node --check src/*.js src/routes/*.js src/middleware/auth.js src/data/store.js` e a verificação concluiu com sucesso.

author: mvillmow
body:
## Summary

New skill documenting how to implement thread-safe data structures in Mojo 0.26.1 using `os.atomic.Atomic` for spinlocks and atomic counters.

- SpinLock implementation using `fetch_add`/`fetch_sub` test-and-set pattern
- Atomic counter struct for lock-free statistics
- Per-bucket locking pattern for pool-style data structures
- Workarounds for Mojo 0.26.1 limitations (Atomic not Movable, comptime format crashes)

## Verification Level

**verified-local**

Tests pass locally (19 tests: 13 existing + 6 concurrent stress tests across 5 consecutive runs with zero flakes). CI validation pending on ProjectOdyssey PR #5118.

## Key Findings

**What Worked**:
- `os.atomic.Atomic[DType.int64]` with `fetch_add`/`fetch_sub`/`load`/`max` for lock-free operations
- Heap-allocated `UnsafePointer[UInt8]` with `bitcast[Atomic[...]]()` to work around Atomic not being Movable
- Per-bucket spinlocks minimize contention across different size classes
- `parallelize[worker](N)` for concurrent stress testing

**What Failed**:
- `Atomic` as struct field → breaks synthesized move/copy constructors
- `comptime` inside structs/fns → crashes `mojo format` parser
- `int()` → not available in Mojo 0.26.1, use `Int()` instead
- `store(value)` → not available as expected on Atomic

## Test Plan

- [x] Validate with `python3 scripts/validate_plugins.py` (1019/1019 pass)
- [ ] Verify skill appears in marketplace
- [ ] Test skill discovery with relevant keywords

author: zendergod
body:
This change adds a dedicated canvas selection mode so users can move windows intentionally without interfering with the normal free-pan workflow.

Before this change, canvas interactions mixed panning, focus, and dragging in a way that made multi-window spatial editing awkward. Users could move some panels opportunistically, but there was no persistent selection mode, no marquee selection flow, and no clean way to drag multiple windows as a group. The result was that arranging the canvas felt imprecise, especially once browser panels and terminal panels were mixed together.

The root cause was that canvas movement logic was still centered around direct node drag entry points rather than a separate selection state. There was also no shared selection state that the rest of the UI could reference, which is why the mode indicator originally lived as a floating canvas pill instead of integrating with the footer controls.

This PR introduces a persistent selection mode toggled with Ctrl+S. In free mode, the canvas remains pan-first. In selection mode, clicking a window selects it, dragging a selected window moves the selected set, and Cmd+drag on empty canvas creates a marquee selection across terminals and browsers. Browser panels also enter a movement-friendly hidden-view state while selection mode is active so they can be repositioned cleanly. The bottom status control now reflects selection mode directly by switching from Free/Snap state to a Select indicator with the live selected count, and clicking that control exits selection mode.

Validation:
- node --test --experimental-strip-types src/lib/canvas-selection.test.ts
- pnpm build
- pnpm lint

Notes:
- pnpm lint still reports one pre-existing warning in src/components/terminal/cell-terminal.tsx for an unused ILink import.

author: jnoecker
body:
## Summary
- **Compact minimap**: Switches from BFS absolute coordinates to direction-based local positioning. East neighbors are always 1 cell right, north always 1 cell up, etc. This fixes both the visual misalignment and broken click-to-navigate.

### Root cause
The WorldLoader BFS assigns 2D grid coordinates to rooms, but collision avoidance can displace rooms from their expected positions. For example, in the `pbrae` zone, `coop_turkey_hall` claims grid position (-1,3) first, forcing `north_patio` to spiral out to (-2,4). This means `north_patio`'s east neighbor (`front_stoop` at (0,3)) appears 2 cells right and 1 cell up instead of directly east — making the node unclickable where users expect it.

### Fix
The compact minimap now builds a `localPos` map from exit directions instead of using stored coordinates. Current room is at center (0,0), its east neighbor at (1,0), north neighbor at (0,-1), etc. The second hop extends from those positions. This guarantees cardinal alignment regardless of BFS grid collisions.

The expanded (full-zone) map continues using absolute coordinates since it needs to show the entire zone layout.

## Test plan
- [ ] Compact minimap: east neighbor is directly right, clickable
- [ ] Compact minimap: all cardinal neighbors at expected positions
- [ ] Compact minimap: 2-hop rooms visible at correct relative positions
- [ ] Click-to-navigate works for all cardinal directions
- [ ] Expanded map still shows full zone layout correctly

author: luishpcosta
body:
## Summary

- Adiciona `quarkus-opentelemetry` aos dois backends Quarkus (`pulsoreal-ingestao-app`, `pulsoreal-streamer-app`), exportando **traces e logs** via OTLP gRPC para o OTel Collector
- Cria stack de observabilidade completa no Docker Compose:
  - **OTel Collector** (`otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.111.0`) — roteador central: traces → Tempo, logs → Loki
  - **Grafana Loki 3.2** — agregador de logs (filesystem storage para PoC)
  - **Grafana Tempo 2.6** — rastreamento distribuído (receiver OTLP gRPC)
  - **Promtail 3.2** — Docker SD, coleta stdout de todos os containers de infra → Loki
- Provisiona datasources **Loki** e **Tempo** no Grafana com correlação trace↔log via `traceId`
- Habilita `LOG_JSON=true` nos containers das apps Quarkus (logs estruturados com `traceId`/`spanId`)
- Adiciona `quarkus-logging-json` ao `pulsoreal-streamer-app` (que ainda não tinha)
- Adiciona OTel Collector ao scrape do Prometheus (`otel-collector:8889`)
- Atualiza `Makefile`: target `infra` inclui os novos serviços; novos alvos `loki-ui` e `tempo-ui`

## Fluxo de sinais

```
Apps Quarkus ──OTLP gRPC──→ otel-collector:4317
                                    │
                        ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                        ▼                       ▼
                     Tempo                    Loki
                   (traces)                  (logs)
                        │                       │
                        └───────────┬───────────┘
                                    ▼
                           Grafana Explore
                       (correlação trace↔log)

Promtail → Docker socket → logs de kafka, emqx, influxdb... → Loki
```

## Como usar após `make infra` ou `make up-app`

```bash
# Verificar backends
curl -s http://localhost:3100/ready   # Loki → "ready"
curl -s http://localhost:3200/ready   # Tempo → "ready"

# Grafana → Explore → selecionar Loki
{job="pulsoreal-ingestao-app"}
{job=~"pulsoreal-.*"} |= "ERROR"

# Grafana → Explore → selecionar Tempo
# Search: service name = pulsoreal-streamer-app
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `make infra` sobe loki, tempo, otel-collector, promtail sem erros
- [ ] `curl -s http://localhost:3100/ready` retorna `ready`
- [ ] `curl -s http://localhost:3200/ready` retorna `ready`
- [ ] `make up-app` sobe os apps Quarkus que se conectam ao otel-collector
- [ ] Grafana Explore → datasource Loki → query `{job="pulsoreal-ingestao-app"}` retorna logs
- [ ] Grafana Explore → datasource Tempo → busca por service name retorna traces
- [ ] Trace no Tempo tem botão "Logs for this span" apontando para Loki

author: mariusae
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #3241
* #3231
* #3228
* #3227
* #3225
* #3215
* #3224
* #3223
* __->__ #3222
* #3209

HostMesh::shutdown and HostMesh::stop now use a two-phase approach:

1. Terminate all user procs concurrently across hosts via a new
   TerminateChildren message. Service infrastructure (host agent,
   comm proc, networking) stays alive so forwarder flushes can
   still reach remote hosts.
2. Shut down/stop hosts concurrently. No user procs remain, so
   this is fast and cannot deadlock on cross-host flush timeouts.

Previously, each host's ShutdownHost handler terminated children
and then tore down networking atomically. Under concurrent shutdown,
one host could destroy its networking while another host's dying
procs were still flushing forwarders to it, causing hangs until
MESSAGE_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT expired.

Also bumps comm test timeouts from 60s to 120s to accommodate
stress-run CPU contention.

Differential Revision: [D98222466](https://our.internmc.facebook.com/intern/diff/D98222466/)

author: mvillmow
body:
## Summary

Documents batch auto-merge + rebase of 14 open PRs and migration of /retrospective and /advise commands from clone-to-.agent-brain pattern to git worktree isolation.

- Batch auto-merge on 14 PRs with error handling for "clean status" and "unstable" edge cases
- Parallel worktree agents (3 agents, 4-5 PRs each) for fast rebase
- Worktree migration pattern: replace clone+rm-rf with git worktree add/remove

## Verification Level

**verified-ci** — All 14 PRs passed CI and merged; worktree migration PR #991 passed CI and merged.

## Key Findings

**What Worked**:
- `gh pr merge --auto --rebase` in bulk loop with retry for "clean status" errors
- 3 parallel worktree-isolated agents rebased 14 PRs in ~2 minutes
- KISS for read-only commands: keep .agent-brain cache, only use worktrees for writes

**What Failed**:
- "clean status" error on first auto-merge attempt (PR already eligible) -> retry
- "unstable status" on PR with pending CI -> wait and retry
- Considered full worktree migration for /advise -> unnecessary for read-only ops

- [ ] Verify skill appears in marketplace

author: vyadavmsft
body:
## Description

VHD-backed VM deployment fails when attaching standard managed data disks

Root cause:
The Azure ARM template split data disk handling into three branches: Ultra SSD disks, imported VHD-backed disks, and ordinary managed disks. After that split, the template only declared Microsoft.Compute/disks resources for Ultra SSD and imported VHD disks. Ordinary Empty managed data disks were still referenced by the VM storage profile using the generated resource name, but no corresponding disk resource existed in the template.

Impact:
Validation failed before deployment for VHD-backed VM scenarios with standard managed data disks with an InvalidTemplate error stating that the expected Microsoft.Compute/disks resource was not defined.

Fix:
Create ordinary non-Ultra, non-imported managed data disks as explicit Microsoft.Compute/disks resources and attach them through the VM storage profile, so all managed data disk paths use consistent resource-backed attachment semantics. Keep imported VHD disks on the dedicated import path and preserve the per-disk imported-data detection introduced for mixed disk sets.

Validation:
Ran focused Azure selftests covering imported data disk generation and ARM template shape:
- AzurePrepareTestCase.test_generate_data_disks_counts_imported_vhds_toward_total
- AzurePrepareTestCase.test_arm_template_handles_imported_data_disks_per_entry

author: mariusae
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #3241
* #3231
* #3228
* #3227
* #3225
* #3215
* #3224
* __->__ #3223
* #3222
* #3209

The two-phase shutdown (phase 1: terminate children, phase 2: tear down
hosts) reduced flaky test failures from ~32% to ~2%. The remaining hangs
occur because TerminateChildren blocks the host agent's message loop
while awaiting destroy_and_wait. If a dying proc's forwarder flush needs
to deliver a message to the host agent (e.g. supervision notifications),
deadlock occurs — the agent is single-threaded and can't process the
incoming message while blocked.

Fix: spawn a TerminationWorker child actor to do the termination work so
the host agent returns immediately and keeps processing messages.

- Add HostAgentState enum (Running/Stopping/Shutdown) replacing
  Option<HostAgentMode>
- Add TerminationWorker child actor that runs terminate_children in
  init(), sends the ack, and returns the host via oneshot channel
- Add TerminationDone handler to recover the host after termination
- StopHost/ShutdownHost skip redundant termination when created is empty

body:
## Summary
- **Remove `continue-on-error: true`** from ruff lint and npm audit in `ci.yml` — these were silently hiding lint and security failures
- **Add fail-on-error step** to `security-checks.yml` — the workflow previously reported bandit/npm-audit/pip-audit results in a summary but never failed the job, so security issues could slip through unnoticed
- **Standardize Node.js versions** to `'20'` across `ci.yml` and `docs.yml` (was mixed `20.x`/`20`)
- **Add missing `@file/@module/@layer` headers** to 7 governance module files per project code style guidelines

## Changes
