author: nkamau12
body:
## Summary

- **Wire `onNodeHover` into ForceGraph3D** — the handler already existed for 2D, now connected in 3D mode too so `hoveredNodeId` state updates correctly
- **Custom `nodeThreeObject` callback (`render3DNode`)** — each node becomes a `THREE.Mesh` with `SphereGeometry` sized by `connectionCount`, `MeshLambertMaterial` colored by cluster, stale nodes at 0.45 opacity, hovered nodes at 1.5× radius with emissive cluster-color glow (intensity 0.3)
- **Depth fog via `onEngineStop`** — applies `THREE.FogExp2(0x0a0f19, 0.008)` to the scene after the physics warmup, fading distant nodes into the dark background for a depth-of-field effect
- **Link improvements**: `linkWidth` raised to 2, `linkDirectionalParticles={2}` added for visual parity with 2D edges

## Implementation notes

Uses a `hoveredNodeIdRef` (synced with `hoveredNodeId` state via `useEffect`) inside the stable `render3DNode` callback. This avoids stale closure issues without forcing a full mesh rebuild on every hover change — the callback reads the ref at call time rather than closing over state.

The `THREE` import is at module level but the module only loads when `viewMode === '3d'` triggers the `lazy()` boundary, so three.js is never parsed in 2D-only sessions.

## Test plan

- [ ] Switch to 3D mode — nodes render as colored spheres sized by connection count
- [ ] Hover a node — it should visibly grow (1.5×) and show a color glow
- [ ] Hover away — node returns to normal size/appearance
- [ ] Stale nodes appear at reduced opacity in 3D
- [ ] Background fog creates depth fade for distant nodes
- [ ] No console errors on hover/unhover cycles
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes (verified clean)
- [ ] 2D mode behavior is completely unchanged

body:
## Context

This PR introduces a `base` field for settings profiles to allow profiles to either overlay `user` settings or to overlay `default`, which is simply zed's defaults (user settings are skipped). I'm not entirely sure I love `default` because it's a bit confusing (there's a setting called `default` but the default is `user`). Another idea I had was `factory` (`user` (default) or `factory`) - curious to hear from the reviewers. This will be useful for those of us who need to quickly flip to a default state, or a default state with some customizations on top. Additionally, from what I can tell, VS Code's profile system is more in line with what this PR is offering in Zed - profiles overlay the default settings, not the user's customization layer. So this will be familiar for those users.

I've had no issue with the migrator, code is pretty simple there, but would love for @smitbarmase to review the migration to make sure I'm not missing something.

## Summary
This PR adds plugin support to the markdown rendering pipeline, allowing plugins to extend and transform markdown output through micromark extensions and HTML transformations.

## Key Changes
- **Plugin parameter**: Added optional `plugins` parameter to `renderMarkdown()` function
- **Micromark extensions**: Plugins can now provide custom micromark syntax and HTML extensions that are composed with the default GFM extensions
- **HTML transformation**: Plugins can define a `transformHtml()` hook that runs after slug link resolution, enabling post-processing of the final HTML output
- **Plugin execution order**: Multiple plugins are applied in the order they are provided, allowing plugins to build on transformations from previous plugins
- **Type safety**: Added import of `ScribePlugin` type to ensure type-safe plugin handling

## Implementation Details
- Plugin micromark extensions are flattened and spread into the extensions array alongside GFM extensions
- HTML transformations are applied sequentially after slug link resolution, ensuring that slug links are already resolved when plugins run
- The function maintains backward compatibility - when no plugins are provided, behavior is identical to before
- Comprehensive test coverage includes: basic extension application, HTML extension handling, plugin ordering, composition of multiple plugins, and interaction with slug link resolution

body:
## Summary

対話生成の構造を改善し、introduction/conclusion をコンテキストとして活用することで、より一貫性のある対話を生成できるようにした。

## 実装内容

- `generate_introduction()`: 導入ナレーションを個別生成
- `generate_conclusion()`: 結論ナレーションを個別生成
- `convert_section()`: `analyze_structure()` 廃止、個別生成方式に変更
- `generate_dialogue()`: プロンプトに導入・結論との連携指示を追加
  - 「導入で述べた内容は繰り返さない」
  - 「結論につながるよう議論を展開する」
- 汎用LLMテスター追加 (`scripts/llm_tester.py`)

## 確認方法

```bash
# 対話変換を実行
make dialogue-convert INPUT=sample/book2.xml

# 出力XMLを確認
cat data/*/dialogue_book.xml | head -100

# LLMテスターで比較検証
python scripts/llm_tester.py --compare scripts/prompts/dialogue_v1.yaml scripts/prompts/dialogue_v2.yaml
```

## 補足

- Issue #61 の議論を経て、パターン2（intro/conclusionをコンテキストとして渡す方式）を採用
- 検証結果: コンテキストありの場合、文字数24%減、結論への接続が強化
- 参考: https://github.com/rengotaku/text-reading-with-llm/issues/61#issuecomment-4130385287

Closes #61

body:
The live Supabase database has a `seller_profiles` table that is missing the `"sellerStatus"` column, causing a PostgreSQL error at runtime for any query or RLS policy that references it.

## Changes

- **`supabase/migrations/010_add_seller_profiles_status.sql`** — idempotent `DO $$` migration that:
  - Creates `public.seller_profiles` (with FK refs to `auth.users` and `public.companies`) if the table doesn't exist
  - Adds `"sellerStatus" text DEFAULT 'pending'` if the table exists but the column is absent
  - Sends `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'` to invalidate the PostgREST schema cache immediately

The column is quoted camelCase (`"sellerStatus"`) to match the exact identifier the application already queries — renaming to snake_case would leave the original error unresolved.

body:
- store and collect base_memory_mb_by_mode per sim mode

As we are introducing exec-driven simulation (https://github.com/litz-lab/scarab-infra/pull/349), we should have different base memory usage per simulation mode.

After running `./sci --sim <json>` with `exec` mode configured in the json,
running `./sci --collect-mem <json>` will update base memory of `exec` in `workloads_db.json`.

When we run a simulation, it should find the correct base memory usage based on the simulation mode.
